audits.title: Classical swine fever

recommendations.text: In view of the prevalence of the disease in wild boar and of the speed with which it can move, largely through the activities of hunters, both within national boundaries and across them, veterinary authorities, even those whose area of responsibility contains only a small population of wild boar, must have in place measures which enable them to identify and deal with any evidence of classical swine fever.

In the context of the fight against swine fever it is not possible to operate effectively with control measures which are activated only at the moment when an outbreak is first identified; they must be in place, with the same level of detail and effectiveness, whether the disease is present or not. 7.2. Recommendations to the German authorities 7.2.1. The mission team recommends, in respect at least of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia, the following: · improvements in the cleaning and disinfection of vehicles used for the transport of pigs; · measures to bring about increased official supervision of pig collection centres; · improved supervision of herd registers; · changes in the procedures in semen collection centres to remove the risk of the dissemination of swine fever virus in semen or by any of the activities concerned in the provision of an artificial insemination service. 7.2.2. The German authorities should provide details of the action taken to implement these recommendations by 31 December 1998 (and notify the Food and Veterinary Office thereof). 7.3. Recommendations to the Commission 7.3.1. Increasing specialisation in agriculture has led to whole areas of Europe being devoted to the same aspect of pig production, with the result that pigs have to be transported in large numbers and often over long distances 9 to provide inputs or to reach markets. The mission team recommends that the Commission consider the possibility of a decision requiring that a period of at least thirty days should separate the introduction of pigs to, and any movement of pigs from, a holding, except for pigs sent for direct slaughter. 7.3.2. The introduction of a policy designed to emphasise regional self- sufficiency is also recommended as it would certainly have as a consequence a reduction in the incidence of classical swine fever and, possibly, of other List A diseases. 10

audits.title: Poultry meat

recommendations.text: The Commission should consider initiating infringement proceedings on the grounds that the EC requirements have not been complied with, in particular regarding the approval of establishments (Council Directive 71/118/EEC), the control of zoonoses (Council Directive 92/117/EEC) and the welfare of laying hens (Council Directive 88/166/EEC).

The Commission should consider developing regulations/guidelines in regard to the amount of supervisory staff required for post mortem inspection taking into account the modern slaughter technology and especially the line speed of slaughter.

The Commission should consider developing guidelines to be used by the Member States in regard to the supervision of fresh poultry meat production. 6.2. Recommendations to the Member State (1) The competent authorities of Germany should rectify the deficiencies found in the different establishments visited and referred to under the different conclusions in Section 5 above. In particular, attention should be paid to the rectification of deficiencies in the field of approval conditions and slaughter hygiene. (2) The competent authorities of Germany should take appropriate measures to rectify any deficiencies of the same type found during this mission in all the other approved establishments in Germany. (3) The competent authorities of Germany should rectify the deficiencies referred to under the different conclusions in Section 5 above concerning the veterinary control on zoonoses and animal welfare of laying hens kept in battery cages.
The competent authorities should address the weaknesses in the supervisory systems at the different levels in order to ensure implementation of the requirements of the legislation in all the Länder.

Within three months after the receipt of the final report the competent authorities of Germany should inform the Commission of the progress and results of the measures taken, including a timetable for completion, within a reasonable period, of measures and actions still outstanding at that time. PAGE 41 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT 1057/2000 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report (1) The C.A. has stated in their letter of 23/5/00 that the Authorities of the Länder concerned have assured that in the 3 establishments visited by the FVO where deficiencies of a more severe nature were noted, immediate action has been undertaken to guarantee the wholesomeness of the meat produced, while the completion of the correction of structural defects in particular is due for a later date. (2) The C.A. has stated in their letter of 15/8/00 that: (a) A list of all registered poultry meat establishments (cfr Art. 7 of Council Directive 71/118/EEC) was forwarded to the Commission. (b) The veterinary presence is now guarantied in two of the poultry slaughterhouses where this shortcoming was noted during the FVO visit. (c) An administrative act concerning the performance of official supervision in accordance with the Meat Hygiene Law and the Poultry Meat Hygiene Law (VwVFlHG/GFlHG) is currently being drawn up, as mentioned at the final meeting in Bonn on 7 April. This will lay down, for the first time, uniform principles at national level concerning supervision activities for the poultry meat sector. (d) Further coordination is ensured, particularly through the joint Federal and Land fora mentioned in the report (meetings of the Federal Government and the Länder, Argevet), working meetings held by the various levels of the veterinary authority in the Länder and training sessions for veterinary supervision staff. The production of poultry meat preparations in a plant which has not been approved for this type of operation constitutes a breach of the Poultry Meat Hygiene Regulation (Geflügelfleischhygiene- Verordnung) and, as such, is duly followed up. (e) The veterinary authorities were notified that the Länder should take the necessary steps to prepare for the official checks conducted in accordance with the Directive 92/117/EEC. General circulars have already been issued by the Länder in this regard PAGE 42

audits.title: Milk and milk-based products

recommendations.text: INTRODUCTION The mission took place in Germany from 28 February to 03 March 2000. The mission team comprised two inspectors from the FVO. The mission was undertaken as part of the FVO's planned mission programme. The inspection team was accompanied during the whole mission by at least one representative from the central CAs. An opening meeting was held on 28 February 2000 with the central CAs and representatives of the CA of the Federal States SH and MV at the BMG. At this meeting, the inspection team confirmed the objectives of and itinerary for the mission, and additional information required for the satisfactory completion of the mission was requested. The final meeting was held 3 March 2000 at BgVV with the CA of the Federal States SH and MV and the BgVV (no representatives of the central CAs participated at this meeting).

OBJECTIVES OF THE MISSION The objective of the mission was to carry out an evaluation of the transposition and application of Council Directive 92/46/EEC laying down the health rules for the production and placing on the market of raw milk, heat-treated milk and milk-based products in Germany. In order to assess the performance of the official control services, visits to several establishments, a farm and laboratories chosen by the CAs were carried out. This was the first mission undertaken in Germany for this purpose. It forms part of a 2-year series of similar missions to all Member States. At the end of this programme a summary report will be issued. In pursuit of this objective, the following sites were visited: COMPETENT AUTHORITY VISITS Central (BMG) 1 Federal States (Land level) 2 LABORATORY VISITS Central/reference 1 Inter-professional laboratory 1 FOOD PROCESSING ESTABLISHMENTS On-farm production of milk based products 1 Caseinate producing establishment 1 Milk processing establishments 1 LIVE ANIMAL CONTROL SITES Farms 1 6

LEGAL BASIS FOR THE MISSION The mission was carried out under the general provisions of Community legislation and, in particular: ·Commission Decision 98/139/EC of 4 February 1998 laying down certain detailed rules concerning on-the-spot checks carried out in the veterinary field by Commission experts in the Member States. ·Council Directive 92/46/EEC of 16 June 1992 laying down the health rules for the production and placing on the market of raw milk, heat-treated milk and milk based products.

recommendations.text: BACKGROUND 4.1. Production and trade information 4.1.1. Milk production in Germany From 1988 to 1997 the number of dairy farms has decreased by 38,2% from 278,300 in 1988 to 172,200 in 1997. Also the number of dairy cows has decreased by 28,1% from 6,992,700 to 5,026,000. However, in the same time period the average production/cow increased by 22,2 % from 4,568 kg to 5,575 kg. Also the average number of cows/dairy farm has increased by 15,9 % from 25,2 to 29,2. In 1999, Germany had a milk quota of 27.8 million tonnes. The central CA (BML) and the CA of SH1 had no separate statistics on the sheep and goat milk production. The main part of this production is used for direct sale or processed further on the farm and sold directly to the consumer. 4.1.2. Dairy industry The production of dairy products in Germany in 1997 is presented in the following table: Product type Amount In % (tonnes) Drinking milk and cream 8165,5 71,2 Condenced milk 566,0 4,9 Butter 442,4 3,9 Cheese 1590,1 13,9 Melted cheese 150,1 1,3 Milk powder 548,0 4,7 Casein/caseinates 10,6 0,09 Total 11.472,7 100 1 See comments of the German CA 7 4.2. Health information 4.2.1. Animal health situation Germany profits from a favourable animal health situation for bovines, sheep and goats: Ø Foot and mouth disease: freedom since 1989 Ø Bovine tuberculosis and brucellosis: Germany is officially free from bovine tuberculosis (Commission Decisions 99/467/EC and 2000/69/EEC) and brucellosis (Commission Decisions 99/466/EC and 2000/69/EEC) and also free from Brucella melitensis (Commission Decision 93/52/EEC). The monitoring of bovine Brucellosis is based on testing of the tank milks every second year with ELISA and of Brucella melitensis on random testing of 5 % of the animals annually. The screening for bovine tuberculosis is based mostly on the post mortem controls. 4.2.2. Food poisonings and zoonoses In 1993-1997, 4,7 % of food poisoning outbreaks were caused by milk and milk products (33/782 outbreaks). Of these outbreaks, 7 were caused by Campylobacter sp.. In 1998, one outbreak (source cheese made from raw milk) was caused by S. aureus. No milk and milk product related data on salmonellosis was available, but the total number of persons with enteritis infections caused by Salmonella serovars in 1999 was 85,015. The number of human brucellosis cases in 1999 was 21, of Q fever 276 and of newborn listeriosis 31 (data published by the federal authority Robert-Koch- Institute). In 1999 there were 2 microbiological alerts for German milk products (both Listeria monocytogenes in cheeses).

MAIN FINDINGS 5.1. Legislation · German national legislation on food hygiene of milk and milk products The basic food hygiene legislation is formed by: Ø LMBG, BGBl. I Nr. 36, p.1169 Framework law on food hygiene with general regulations, orders and prohibitions for protection of the consumers against health dangers and deceptions. Ø Verordnung über Lebensmittelhygiene und zur Änderung der Lebensmitteltransportbehälter-Verordnung (Ordinance on Food hygiene and to Change of the Ordinance of food transport containers, BGBl. I Nr. 56, p. 2008) More specific regulations on food hygiene. Council Directive 92/46/EEC is transposed into German law by: · MVO of 24 April 1995 (BGBl. I Nr. 21 of the 3.5.1995, p. 544) and · MGVO of 9 July 1980 (BGBl. I Nr. 36 of the 12.7.1980, p. 878). 8 · Comparison of the German legislation with the EU legislation The German legislation on milk hygiene differs in some points from Council Directive 92/46/EEC2: 1. Establishments selling heat-treated milk, butter and certain cheeses (Hard, semi-hard and soft cheeses) to retail shops do not need an approval (para 20 point 2 of MVO, mittelbare Abgabe an den Verbraucher). 2. The definition for direct sale includes also selling of products on the local weekly markets (Wochenmärkte). 3. The requirement for the on-the-spot treatment of milk from sheep and goats deriving from holdings not free of Brucella melitensis has not been transcribed. This has however no practical consequences, as Germany is free from the disease. 4. The definition of thermisised milk as far as the duration of the heat treatment is concerned differs from the provisions of Council Directive 92/46/EEC. 5. Germany has included in its legislation the possibility to approve establishments which are not on the list of establishments from which Member States are allowed to import milk and milk products in the approved third countries. However, this possibility is not practised.

Art. 27 of Council Directive 92/46/EEC has not been transcribed into the national milk hygiene legislation. However, BgVV and BafM have been designated as the NRLs and this has also been notified to the Community.
The sanitary register, as required in Directive 96/23/EC, Art. 10, is not completely transposed into the national legislation.
Council Directive 96/43/EC was not yet transcribed in SH (however, the transposition process was on its way and transposition was completed on the 22.3.2000).

The Milk Hygiene Ordinance contains specific rules for manufacturers who sell non-heat-treated raw milk either directly from the farm to the consumer or as certified milk (Vorzugsmilch). At the place for the sale of raw milk it has to be indicated by a sign that the milk should be boiled before consumption. Certified milk undergoes regular bacteriological controls on pathogens and can be put on the market only as packed ready for sale.
In the definition of composite milk products, which cannot otherwise be classified, the product's dry weight components have to consist of at least 50 % of milk and milk based components.

Ice-cream is defined as a milk product, if it contains milk and milk-based products, irrespective of their amounts. 2 See comments of the German CA 9 5.2. Competent Authority 5.2.1. General structure of the German CA At the federal level, the veterinary services responsible for the co-ordination of all the activities concerning the policy and the implementation of Council Directive 92/46/EEC fall under the responsibility of 2 Ministries, BMG and BML. BMG is in general responsible for the transposition of the Directive 92/46/EEC and has issued the primary legislation for this purpose. BML is responsible for the transposition of the legislation concerning raw milk quality control and has issued primary legislation for this purpose. The application of Council Directive 92/46/EEC is under the responsibility of the Federal States (Länder) (total number 16), each of which has its own Government (Landesregierung). The local CAs are formed by the Districts (Kreise). The total number of Kreises in Germany is 439. In some Federal States an intermediate level, "Bezirksregierung or Regierungspräsidium", exists between the Federal State and the Kreis level (total number 32). The SVUs (total number 36), operating under the supervision of the Federal States, form a part of the veterinary administration. Ø Audits In none of the CA levels visited, were systems of audits applied in the field of milk hygiene. 5.2.2. Central level Ø BMG The BMG and its Directorate of Veterinary Medicine, Division 422 (Foodstuff of Animal Origin) is responsible for the co-ordination of all the activities concerning the policy and the implementation for Directive 92/46/EEC. Within BMG 4 veterinary officers work in Division 422, of whom 1.5 work mostly with milk hygiene matters. Division 422 is also responsible for the co-ordination of the Rapid Alert System and receives and transmits the messages between the Commission and the responsible CA in the Federal State. Responsibilities for the official control of drinking water and of residue monitoring are in the same Ministry but fall under the responsibility of other Divisions. Ø BML The BML and its Directorate Market Policy, Division 423 (General and special aspects of the milk market) is, inter alia, responsible for legislative activities on the raw milk quality at the farm level. The number of staff working within the unit for milk market is 7, of which 1 deals half-time with raw milk quality aspects. The BML maintains the Federal Dairy Research Centre in Kiel, which also functions as a NRL for milk and milk products (see 5.4.2). 10 Ø BgVV Ø General description of responsibilities BgVV is a scientifically orientated and independent superior federal authority with both administrative and scientific tasks. It is responsible to the BMG. Ø Special tasks related to Directive 92/46/EEC The BgVV is responsible for the official compilation of procedures for sampling and testing foods and additives (Amtliche Sammlung von Untersuchungsverfahren according to para 35 of LMBG). The official published compilation was available. The procedures are defined through co-operation between experts from the food control authorities, consumers, science and the industry concerned. Within BgVV one veterinary officer is working with the aspects of milk hygiene. BgVV has been named as the NRL for milk and milk products (see 5.4.2.). Ø Training and publications BgVV organises annually 2 one-day seminars for the veterinary officers and other staff working in the field of food hygiene. For 2000 one seminar is planned on salmonellosis, the other on safety of foodstuffs.3 BgVV has launched several milk hygiene-related publications/press releases in the recent years, which the mission team received. 5.2.3. The Federal State level (Bundesländer) The Federal State level is responsible for the planning, supervision and co- ordination of the application of Council Directive 92/46/EEC. The description of the findings is based on the visits of two states: SH and MV. In these two Federal States, the CA consisted of the central Federal State (Land) level and the local Kreis level. In SH and MV the organisation of the CA responsible for the application of Council Directive 92/46/EEC differed from each other. SH ­ divided responsibilities: · MUNF: In charge of all aspects except raw milk quality control · MLRLLT: In charge of raw milk quality control · MV - MELFF in charge of all aspects of dairy hygiene control. 3 See comments of the German CA 11 The following table summarises the situation in SH and MV: Organisation SH SH MV MV MUNF MLRLLT MELFF MELFF Area of responsibility Milk hygiene Raw milk Milk hygiene Raw milk (excluding raw quality (excluding raw quality Own legislation on milk milk quality control milk quality control hygiene (more precise than control) control) the national legislation) Yes Yes Yes Yes Number of staff in the Ministry 2 21/2 2 3 Number of SVUs (with 1 (with 2 1 (with 2 1 (LKV) accredited laboratories) external sites) external sites) agricultural centre Number of subordinated 14 17 local CA (districts or towns) Number of approved 40 20 establishments Number of plants with 0/0* 0/1 derogations according to Art 8.2 or 11of Directive 92/46/EEC Approval of plants Yes Yes Financing of approvals Fixed fee Fixed fee *In SH in practice plants exist with derogations but these derogations are not mentioned in the approvals (plant visited had wooden shelves for cheese maturation)4. Ø Co-ordination of activities The Ministries at the Federal State level in both SH and MV held regular meetings at least twice annually with the local CA, of which minutes were available. When new legislation was drafted, the district CA were consulted. In SH no inspection and sampling data about the approved establishments was available. Thus the CA at the Federal State level was not able to assess and compare the performance of the district CA. However, the CA of SH had recently started to collect centrally the results and documentation of these inspections. audits.title: Epidemio-surveillance of BSE

recommendations.text: Actions have been taken to enforce BSE-surveillance in Bavaria (enhanced controls, intensified training, monitoring of different levels in the veterinary administration is planned and the recruitment of additional staff).

Since the end of November 2000 a clear procedure to be followed by the laboratories involved has been laid down for possible results (negative, doubtful, positive) from rapid post mortem tests. Regarding identification and registration of bovine animals 1) A separate interface has been installed, which makes it possible to search for all offspring stored in the central database relating to a particular bovine identification number (e.g. an individual cow). 2) Since the end of November 2000 all regional databases are on the same level as regards implementing a priori checks (plausibility checks at the time of entering data in the database).
The follow-up of discrepancies within the sets of data has started.

In the light of the FVO´s conclusions, the Bavarian authorities have taken measures to intensify controls and to correct deficiencies observed during the mission. Regarding Feed-ban: 1) The number of inspectors conducting official feedingstuff controls in Bavaria has increased by 20. 2) Actions have been taken to enforce control on the feed ban (intensified sampling) in Bavaria. 3) Actions have been taken to re-establish microscopical examination of feedingstuffs in Bavaria. 40

audits.title: Classical swine fever

recommendations.text: To the Community Reference Laboratory at the Institute of Virology of the Hanover Veterinary School · To complete the implementation of a comprehensive quality management system and to receive official accreditation of the laboratory. · To reinforce the efforts for further standardisation of the diagnostic procedures for CSF with special regard to the differential diagnosis by NPLA and the application of PCR in routine diagnosis of CSF. · To consolidate the evaluation and presentation of the results of the annually performed inter-laboratory tests. · To maintain the training activities for Central and Eastern European countries but also to reinforce the training activities for the laboratory experts from the Member States.

To the Commission Services · To provide for a proper balance between the duties of the CRL for CSF imposed by Community legislation and the financial assistance granted to the CRL by the Community. · To take into consideration on the occasion of the next revision of Council Directive 80/217/EEC an amendment of the Directive with a view to oblige the national classical swine fever laboratories to provide the CRL with infected organ material in case of primary outbreaks and to oblige the national classical swine fever laboratories to participate in the annually performed inter-laboratory tests organised by the CRL for CSF. · To take into consideration on the occasion of the next revision of Council Directive 80/217/EEC a revision of Annex VI defining the functions and duties of the CRL for CSF with a view to include as specific tasks the assessment of commercially available diagnostic test kits and the molecular epidemiology of CSF. 9. audits.title: Game (wild and farmed) and rabbit meat

recommendations.text: To take urgent action to bring national legislation into line with the relevant EU Directives.
To prepare and implement documented systems for the monitoring of the performance of the official services at the different levels in the Länder
To introduce additional controls to ensure the correct use of health marks.
To ensure that all wild boars shot for human consumption undergo trichinellosis testing.

To correct the deficiencies identified at the establishments visited, and to ensure that all other game and rabbit processing establishments comply with the requirements of the relevant EU legislation. ADDENDUM TO THE MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/1233/2000 Competent authority response to the recommendations in the report The German competent authorities commented upon the report in a letter dated 20 February 2001. A preliminary response to certai s in the report has been forwarded by the Federal Competent authority and by the Veterinary authorities in the Länder involved during the mission. · Federal competent authority The need for further legislation (either on animal disease control or animal welfare) to register rabbit holdings and monitor movements of rabbits intended for food production is under examination. recommendations.text: To Germany It is recommended that the Competent Authorities in Germany: 8.1.1.Provide a response within one month of receipt of the translated final report, giving details of the actions, taken and planned to address the deficiencies relating to the facilities (construction only) referred to in this report; along with a timetable for completion of these actions. § All deficiencies related to the construction of the facilities should be corrected within six months of receipt of the translated final report. In particular storage rooms for NHC-products at ambient and chilled temperature must be put in place. 8.1.2.Provide a response within one month of receipt of the translated final report, giving details of the actions, taken and planned to address the other deficiencies referred to in this report (general findings, BIP staff, hygiene, procedure, equipment, registration, transit, animal welfare, identification and selection and use of the facilities) along with a timetable for completion of these actions. In any event all deficiencies should be corrected within 3 months of receipt of the translated final report and in particular: § BIP staff: Staff should be given the possibility of adequate training in particular in relation to the import procedures and systems for identification and selection of consignments. § Hygiene: Hygiene and maintenance must be improved. § Procedures: Systems containing information on incoming and outgoing consignments must be improved in the BIP, in order to guarantee that all consignments from third countries arriving in the BIPs are under the supervision of the official veterinarians and are checked in accordance with the import requirements to this and the official veterinarian must have full access to these systems. To consider setting up a control-system in order to ensure that veterinary checks on consignments of live animals and products are carried out in accordance with the requirements laid down in Directive 97/78/EC and Directive 91/496/EEC and related Decisions. 21/02/01 - 29649 16 DG(SANCO)/1290/2000 - MR Final § Use of the facilities: The facilities in the Customs building must be dedicated as a priority for the BIP activities.

audits.title: Pesticides

recommendations.text: The competent authorities in Germany should ensure that the results of controls on the marketing and use of plant protection products are reported to the Member States and the Commission in compliance with Article 17 of Directive 91/414/EEC.

The competent authorities in Bavaria and Saxony should ensure that all retailers of plant protection products are inspected regularly. These inspections 21 should include sampling and formulation analysis and should ensure that unauthorised/prohibited products are not sold.
The competent authorities in Germany should ensure that farmers only use authorised plant protection products.

The competent authorities in Germany should establish clear procedures to communicate and trigger rapid alerts and, if necessary, to adapt the control and surveillance of pesticide residues. These procedures should be based on a risk assessment carried out according to toxicological criteria.
The competent authorities in Germany should ensure that laboratory results are communicated quickly to allow seizure of commodities if necessary.

The competent authorities in Germany should ensure that infringement procedures regarding pesticide residues are carried out more quickly and result in appropriate action, including communication with other services concerned. An action plan in response to the recommendations of chapter 7.1, points (1), (2), (3), (4), (5) and (6) should be forwarded to the Commission within 2 months of dispatch of the final report. This action plan should clearly set out the manner and deadline by which the Competent Authorities will address each recommendation. 7.2. To the Commission Services (1) The Commission Services should ensure that the results of controls on the marketing and use of plant protection products reported by the Member States (in compliance with Article 17 of Directive 91/414/EEC) are compiled and evaluated every year. The feedback from Commission Services to Member States, requested by German competent authorities at the closing meeting, should be noted. (2) The Commission Services should continue to support the Member States with a harmonised approach to the assessment of pesticide residue risk and to the use of the Rapid Alert System for Food. 8. ADDENDUM Competent authorities of Germany commented the recommendations of chapter 7.1, point (4) and chapter 7.2, point (2): "Germany has on several occasions referred, in the EC committees, to the need for a harmonised rapid alert system. The Commission has had before it since 1999 a paper drafted by the Standing Committee on Plant Protection Products (Ständiger Ausschuss Pflanzenschutzmittel) aimed at accelerating this harmonisation process. In order to be able to work effectively with it, the Commission must complete various Annexes in this draft paper, since the Commission alone has access to the necessary data. If Germany were to set about devising its own criteria, this would run counter to the harmonisation process." 22

audits.title: Residues in live animals and animal products

recommendations.text: To the competent authorities of Germany To set up an immediate action plan with the aim: · To ensure that Council Directive 96/23/EC and Council Directive 90/167/EEC are fully transposed into national legislation. · To ensure that the controls on the distribution of veterinary drugs are strengthened and in compliance with EC legislation and in particular that the actual practice of veterinarians to dispense premixes directly to the animal owners for the purpose of "Hofmischungen" is suspended. · To ensure that the National Reference Laboratory for residues becomes fully operational. · To ensure that the described serious deficiencies of the routine laboratories as regards the implementation of quality assurance measures and the availability of validated operational methods are addressed in a satisfactory manner. · To ensure that the other deficiencies described in the report are addressed in a satisfactory manner. This immediate action plan including a timescale for the expected completion of the different actions should be submitted to the European Commission within 1 month of receipt of the final report.

To the Commission Services To take into consideration whether formal action against Germany is required in respect of the non-transposition and non-enforcement of Community legislation. 31 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT 3267/2001 Competent Authority Response to the recommendation in the report The German authorities stated in their written comments (dated 12.10.2001) on a draft version of this report that: An Article Act extending the Fleischhygienegesetz, Geflügelfleischhygienegesetz and Lebensmittel- und Bedarfsgegenständsegesetz is currently being prepared with a view to further transpose Directive 96/23/EC. Some of the provisions will be incorporated into the law directly (e.g. those applicable to slaughter) whereas in other cases provisions will be made for corresponding implementing regulations. It has been planned to incorporate the measures to be taken in the event of positive residue findings and other regulations into national legislation. Immediate action has been taken concerning the list of pre-mixes: four preparations were withdrawn with immediate effect and in a further 41 cases authorisation was relinquished by the holder, remaining stocks will have to be disposed of by June 2003. The problem of "Hofmischung" will be addressed by amendments to the current regulations on medicinal products. All premixes containing combinations of bacteriostatic and bacteriocide antibiotics are currently being examined as part of the authorisation renewal procedure. Concerning the staffing of the ZERL, the Federal Government is currently taking the necessary measures to enable it to perform its function satisfactorily. The BMVEL is working on obtaining the budget resources to enable the BgVV to take its full responsibilities as the national reference laboratory. Each visited Bundesland has also given extensive comments on changes already made and planned for the future to improve the control system regarding residues in live animals and animal products. Full evaluation of the action taken and planned is possible only after receipt of a comprehensive action plan from the German authorities. 32

audits.title: BSE

recommendations.text: The German competent authorities should follow up without delay the recommendations made in the previous report (DG(SANCO)1129/2000) and in particular: · all involved parties should be encouraged to notify BSE suspects clearly indicating the suspicion. 33 · the BSE definition in national legislation should be amended in order to comply with Commission Decision 98/272/EC. 8.3. Epidemio-surveillance 1. The German competent authorities should take action in order to decrease substantially the number of autolytic samples in fallen stock ensuring in particular that fallen stock are promptly notified.

The information flow between the competent authorities at state and federal level should be improved. In particular the federal competent authorities should ensure that all data concerning the animals tested in the framework of the monitoring programme are reliable and made available to the Commission Services.

The competent authorities of the states should ensure that official cross checks on the age of animals are performed in slaughterhouses in order to monitor the eligibility/exclusion of animals for/from the BSE monitoring programme.

The federal competent authorities should bring the provision for emergency slaughter in line with European legislation by ensuring that an ante-mortem inspection is always carried out. 8.4. Total feed ban 1. The German competent authorities should take measures to ensure that fishmeal is channelised from the point of production/entry (border inspection post) to authorised feed mills and stores. 2. The competent authorities of Bremen should ensure that the import procedures for fishmeal are correctly applied. 3. The competent authorities of the states of Brandenburg and Lower Saxony should consider increasing the number of staff to make sure that the feed ban can be properly monitored. 8.5. Specified Risk Material 1. The competent authorities of the states should ensure that official cross checks on the age of animals are performed in slaughterhouses in order to monitor the removal of SRM of all bovines aged more then 12 months. 2. A system should be implemented to ensure vertebral columns of cattle older than 12 months of age are removed at cutting plant and retail level. 3. The competent authorities of Lower Saxony should ensure that spinal cords are properly removed under official supervision and Specified Risk Material is properly stained. 4. The competent authorities of the states should issue instructions and take measures to ensure reconciliation of Specified Risk Material throughout the whole chain from removal to disposal. 34 9. ADDENDUM TO THE MISSION REPORT DG (SANCO) 3302/2001 German competent authorities response to the recommendations in the report German competent authorities stated in their comments that: 1. The States visited have notified that the shortcomings have been rectified 2. As regards the notification of BSE suspects a letter was sent to the senior Land veterinary authorities, which in turn reminded all parties concerned of the need for a well-organised BSE surveillance system and, to pay particular attention to clinical suspicions of the disease. 3. The definition of BSE suspects will be amended according to the Regulation 999/2001 in the context of the new German TSE monitoring regulation, in the meantime the definition reported in the above mentioned Regulation applies also in German since 1 July 2001 as directly applicable. 4. States visited implemented cross-checks on age of animals in order to monitor the eligibility/exclusion of animals for/from the BSE monitoring programme.
Federal authorities are drafting an amendment to the Meat Hygiene Act, which will ensure that an ante-mortem inspection is always carried out on animals emergency slaughtered.

Competent authority in the port of Bremen immediately took emergency measures to rectify the shortcomings observed by recruiting additional staff and raising the budget. Bremen now has a system which ensures the proper channelling of fishmeal via EU stores from the place of production or importation to approved feed mills.
Competent authorities in Brandenburg and Lower Saxony acknowledged actions to increase the number of staff in the framework of the feed ban monitoring.
In Lower Saxony the official veterinarians were provided with written instructions specifying their tasks in the context of controls of removal and staining of SRM.

A joint project of the Bund (Federal Institute for Meat Research and Federal Institute for Consumer Health Protection and Veterinary Medicine) and the Land of Lower Saxony concerning alternative slaughtering techniques (vacuuming of the spinal cord before splitting the carcasses) should contribute to resolving the difficulties mentioned. . 35

audits.title: Feeding of swill to farm animals and waste food from prohibited sources

To the Commission Services 8.2.1. To monitor the action plan requested of the German authorities, and to take any necessary consequential action. 29 In response to the draft report, the German Competent Authorities stated that further analysis was not required, since standard federal rules apply equally in all Länder. audits.title: Fishery products and live bivalve molluscs

recommendations.text: Legislation i : Schleswig-Holstein has changed its testing procedures to detect faecal coliforms ii : Since the Commission Decision 2002/225/EC entered into force, Schleswig-Holstein has anticipated alignment of the Fish Hygiene Order, assessing the level of DSP toxins (okadaic acid, DTX) against the 160 µg/kg limit, referred to total shellfish flesh.

National Reference Laboratories i : The official application for accreditation was submitted in mid-May 2002 and an inspection by the accreditation body is expected in October 2002. ii, iii, iv : The national official laboratories in Germany cannot be instructed by the NRL since the constitution gives the Länder sole competence for implementation of food law. The NRLs are responsible only for coordination, which they already started to intensify. Moreover, there will be more intense coordination of the flow of information between the NRL and the Länder authorities responsible for testing of bivalve molluscs. This particularly applies to positive test findings by the district offices and the subsequent measures, such as closure and reopening of harvesting areas and RAFFS reports.

Official control Bivalve molluscs Competent authority: i : The NRLs are trying to extend their testing activities in order to build up practical experience. For constitutional reasons, however, they cannot perform official food control activities or issue instructions to the Länder laboratories responsible for official food control testing, but must limit themselves to a co-ordination role. ii : . Because of the current legal situation, use of the mouse bioassay cannot be made compulsory in Germany. Animal tests are permitted only if they are essential in the current state of the art and if the aim pursued cannot be achieved by non-animal methods. Since adequately validated alternative methods are available (HPLC for DSP and a fluorimetry and HPLC method for PSP), the mouse bioassay is not necessary. In the view of the German experts, the chemical analysis methods used in the Länder testing laboratories afford health protection at least equivalent to that of the mouse bioassay. Parts of molluscs from other Member States which had been tested with the mouse bioassay in the country of origin and classed as safe have thus repeatedly been identified as hazardous to health and withdrawn from sale using the chemical methods employed in 12 Germany. The NRL for marine biotoxins had noted that, while standards are not available for all individual compounds from the groups of marine biotoxins, this is not necessary for many minor components in view of their fairly low toxicity. Classification iii : Schleswig-Holstein reports that the persons concerned have received training in the sampling method and sample transport has been optimised. For the coming harvesting season, the following procedure will be adopted where the microbiological findings are unsatisfactory: ­ immediate testing of a second sample; ­ if the finding is confirmed, the area's status as a harvesting zone is suspended until three successive samples are satisfactory.

Written guarantees In addition to the above mentioned preliminary reactions and guaranties, specific information related to corrective actions undertaken by the relevant CAs in establishments has been supplied. Further more, in the Cuxhaven veterinary institute (Lower Saxony), the prescribed MPN number method has now been introduced for E. Coli testing, after briefing by the NRL.

audits.title: Mycotoxyn contamination, import controls on products of plant origin, and in particular for the assessment of mycotoxin and 3-MCPD contamination and monitoring of irradiated foodstuffs

recommendations.text: The Competent Authority should take measures to ensure that import controls on foodstuffs of plant origin are reviewed and strengthened, particularly where non-compliance is suspected, in order to attain a level of official controls at the appropriate stage which will prevent risks to public health within the meaning of Council Directive 89/397/EEC. Consignments monitoring should increase and the Competent Authority in charge of food of plant origin should be involved in carrying out checks regularly. Given the considerable information existing on recurrent contaminant findings, the controls should cover a broader variety of products of plant origin.
Implementation of Commission Decisions should not be delayed.
The procedure to update and communicate goods to be imported that are submitted to certain requirements according to specific circulars under Article 48 of LMBG should be clearly established.
Customs decisions taken on a rejected consignment should be notified to other border posts to avoid different treatment.
The Competent Authority should take measures to ensure that accurate data regarding consignments of food commodities are available to the Authority in charge of import controls.
The Competent Authorities should ensure that declarations concerning imported peanuts are under the appropriate TARIC codes.

The Competent Authority should supervise private sampling to ensure the enforcement of legislative provisions. The Competent Authority should take measures to ensure that the results of tests carried out in private laboratories are notified to the competent official body. Laboratory performance should be assessed to evaluate the impact of rejection rate differences.
The Competent Authority should take measures to ensure that all rejected consignments are promptly notified to the RASFF.
The Competent Authority should take the necessary measures in the event of non-compliance to ensure that contaminated goods within the scope of the mission are not forwarded to other EU destinations.

Import controls on foodstuffs potentially exposed to ionising radiation should include foodstuffs of plant origin. A programme in response to these recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission Services within two months after the receipt of the final report. The Competent Authority should provide detailed information on the actions that will be taken and propose deadlines by which such actions will be completed. 28 8.2. To the European Commission Services It is recommended that the Commission services should consider the following actions in respect of the identified conclusions: (1) Delays in the implementation of Commission Decisions regarding some contaminants should be addressed to avoid differences in enforcement in Member States. (2) The Commission should consider difficulties that may arise from customs declarations of goods under TARIC codes not explicitly mentioned in Commission Decisions. (3) The issues raised in the mission conclusion 6.4 regarding the movement of goods for customs release at weaker points of control should be addressed in future FVO mission plans. 9. ADDENDUM The German Competent Authorities commented on the draft report by letter dated 22 July 2002. In their response they proposed a large number of factual corrections, some of which have been incorporated in the final text. They asked that recommendations, in particular (6), (7) and (9) be reconsidered as to their plausibility in view of the corrections to the report. 29

audits.title: Classical swine fever in Rhineland-Palatinate

recommendations.text: To take immediate action to transpose Council Directive 2001/89/EC into national legislation.
Implement the provisions of Council Directive 64/432/EEC in relation to the computer database for the registration of pig holdings and for movements of pigs.
Increase the sampling intensity for internal pig movements, in the event of a worsening of the CSF situation in Rhineland-Palatinate.
Identify and implement a reliable means to estimate the feral pig population, using a combination of different parameters such as "hunting bag" and demographic parameters.

Collect and analyse data according to the recommendations of the CSF Manual and the Report of the Scientific Committee on Animal Health and Animal Welfare adopted 10 August 1999 DG XXIV/B3/R09/1999 (Classical Swine Fever in Wild Boar).
Introduce effective controls over traceability and contamination of feral pig carcasses at game collection centres.
Revise the procedures in place at local level, which led to the shortcomings identified in the management of outbreaks 2002/08, 2002/09 and 2002/11.

Keep under continuous review the measures in place to control classical swine fever in Rhineland-Palatinate in light of the changes in the epidemiological situation. The German authorities should amend the plans for the eradication of classical swine fever and the emergency vaccination of feral pigs against classical swine fever in Rhineland Palatinate, taking into full account the conclusions and recommendations of this mission, and submit them to the Commission for further approval, as necessary. The German authorities should submit an action plan indicating the action proposed or already taken, within one month of receiving the final translated report. This plan should include deadlines by which the proposed action will be completed. 17 9.2. To the Commission Services To evaluate the information provided by the German authorities and any changes proposed by them to the above plans in light of this report, and to amend, if necessary, the Decision for the eradication of CSF and vaccination of feral pigs against Classical Swine Fever in the Länder Rhineland- Palatinate. ADDENDUM The German authorities provided comments on the draft report and an initial reaction to some of its recommendations in a letter dated 3 April 2003 (received by the FVO on 24 April). Where appropriate, these comments are reflected in the final report. In respect of the individual recommendations addressed in this reply, the following should be noted: Rec. 9.1.1. An Order, implementing Council Directive 2001/89/EC, should be adopted in May 2003. Rec. 9.1.2. The national authorities have stated that the cattle database was extended to include information on pig holdings in 2000. From 20 December 2002, pig holdings could be registered in the database. However, they noted that some Länder had experienced difficulties in transmitting non-electronic registrations Rec. 9.1.4. The regional authorities of Rhineland-Palatinate have asked the Forschungsanstalt für Waldökologie und Forstwirtschaft to develop a method for estimating the wild boar population and its annual increase. Rec. 9.1.8. Plans are reported to be updated by the Rhineland-Palatinate authorities on the basis of the latest developments and findings. 18

audits.title: Animal welfare

recommendations.text: The CCA should examine the transport of cattle on two deck vehicles, considering the constraints of maximum vehicle height on German roads and the requirement for adequate ventilation above the animals when they are in a naturally standing position (Council Directive 91/628/EEC, Annex, Chapter IA, 2b).

The CCA should encourage the use of a consistent methodology for inspections implementing Article 8 of Council Directive 91/628/EEC. In this context, consideration should be given to the classification of non-conformities established by the "gentlemen's agreement".

The local level in all Länder should ensure that adequate resources, including manpower and training, are available to improve the effectiveness of checks of animal transport. 21 In their response to the draft report the German Authorities accepted the selection procedure for slaughterhouse visits, involving lists supplied in advance of the mission. However, suggestions from the Länder authorities regarding the suitability of the establishments should be taken into account and thus avoid disagreements during the mission and unnecessary organisational expenditure. 15
Additional measures should be taken to deter the transport of sick or injured cows, which does not comply with the requirements of Article 3(b) of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended).

The CCA should initiate an investigation into the overall level of compliance with the requirements for water and feed in slaughterhouses (Council Directive 93/119/EC, Annex A, II, 9). Where necessary, measures should be taken to correct deficiencies.

Regarding the stunning of animals: (a) Continue to develop the system of supervisory checks on the effectiveness of stunning (Council Directive 93/119/EC, Article 6, 1). (b) Ensure that all electrical stunning equipment has the necessary devices (Council Directive 93/119/EC, Annex C II, 3A 2c). 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG (SANCO)/9038/2003 The CA comments on the draft report provide the following initial reaction to several of the recommendations: Regardi The transport of cattle on two deck vehicles is considered to satisfy both the requirement for adequate ventilation above the animals and that for maximum vehicle height. Regardi The CA have found that the objective can be achieved without immediately resorting to harsh punitive measures. Animal welfare legislation is implemented without being influenced by possible economic considerations. Regardi (a) In future, all criteria will be taken into account when recording assessment criteria for effectiveness of stunning. 16

recommendations.text: To continue the development of the epizootic disease task force and to ensure that all contingency plans are updated in line with the recommendations made.

To make more use of the development of possible disease scenarios in the validation and improvement of the CPs at Federal and Land level.

To consider the establishment of stand-by contracts or of a national bank to ensure the supply of ELISA testing equipment. 14 The German authorities should submit an action plan indicating the actions taken and planned in response to the conclusions and recommendations of this report, within two months of receipt of the final, translated version of this report. audits.title: Pesticides - control systems for the placing on the market and use of plant protection products and for pesticide residues in foodstuffs of plant origin; follow up on the recommendations made in the report DG (SANCO) 3227/2001

recommendations.text: The competent authorities should transpose and enforce all EU legislation fully in accordance with the directives and within specified timelines.

The competent authorities should introduce co-ordinated and comprehensive inspection and enforcement procedures for controlling the marketing of plant protection products, including follow-up, in accordance with Article 17 of Council Directive 91/414/EEC.

The competent authorities should establish co-ordinated and comprehensive controls of the uses of plant protection products, including follow-up, in accordance with Article 17 of Council Directive 91/414/EEC.
The competent authorities should plan and significantly increase the number of samples of plant protection products being analysed for composition.
The competent authorities should consider the introduction of controls for the safe disposal of unauthorised plant protection products in long-term storage.

The competent authorities should ensure that Maximum Residue Levels are established for all active substances on the German market at the time of first authorisation of plant protection products containing those substances, in accordance with Article 4.1 (f) of Council Directive 91/414/EEC.
In cases of MRL infringements, the competent authorities should put in place a systematic follow-up procedure to ensure that enforcement and follow-up actions are taken without delay.

The competent authorities should ensure that the analytical uncertainty, established using analytical quality control data of the laboratory, is taken into account in the estimation of consumer risk, in accordance with Commission Directive 2002/63. Furthermore, the analytical screens should include all metabolites included in the harmonised EU residue definitions.
The competent authorities should establish written procedures for the functioning of the Rapid Alert System in Germany.

The competent authorities should consider following SANCO Guideline Documents 223/2000, rev. 9 concerning parallel imports; 3103/2000 (as revised by document 10476/2003) and 825/00, rev. 7 concerning pesticide residue analysis. An action plan in response to the recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission within 2 months of dispatch of the final translated report. This action plan should clearly set out the manner and deadline by which the competent authorities will address each recommendation. 25 9. recommendations.text: Community legislation is transposed within the time-frame laid down in the legislation, and that the application forms always include an up to date list of regulated material.

Increasing the level of training available to inspectors on plant passport related issues.

Whether Bemisia tabaci found on planting material recently imported from non-European countries, should at least on a precautionary basis, be classified as non-European and therefore be subject to eradication measures. In response to recommendation (4), the single authority stated that "the competent authorities in the Länder will once again inform the establishments concerned about the procedures for handling plant passports, will monitor compliance...and will step up these checks if necessary". In response to advisory point (7), the single authority stated that "measures to improve training are being considered". In response to advisory point (8), the single authority stated that "the Länder welcome the introduction of guidelines for inspections" and that "the Heads of Department of the "Agricultural Production" units of the Bund and the Länder have now given their approval for cross- Länder funding to be available for a period of one year to compile a compendium for plant health controls, with the participation and coordination of the BBA. In response to advisory point (8), the single authority noted that "Rhineland- Palatinate has informed us that the plant health service has already given this some thought and that internal monitoring and prognostic measures hence now exist and are being implemented in the ornamental plant establishment visited....Saxony and Thuringia have assured us that measures will be taken in the event of an outbreak of the virus". 19

recommendations.text: To adapt the NPCDB in order to fully comply with Article 14 §3C of Council Directive 64/432/EEC and ensure that the system provides quick and reliable traceability in case of an outbreak.

To implement corrective measures in order to ensure that in the Landkreis visited in Lower Saxony, the procedures in case of suspicion of CSF in domestic pigs are consistently applied in accordance with the requirements of Art. 4, paragraph 2, of Council Directive 2001/89/EC and to ensure that a uniform approach is applied at national level.
To ensure that all wild game meat placed on the market has been obtained fulfilling the requirements of Council Directive 92/45/EEC including Art.3 1.b.
To reinforce training and awareness activities for private and official veterinarians.

recommendations.text: Review national MLODs established for Group A substances and ensure that these are commensurate with the detection of abuse and are in line with the target values suggested by the relevant Community Reference Laboratories.

Improve clarity in the construction of the plan to allow a clear distinction to be made between obligatory and voluntary analyte matrix combinations and ensure that all laboratories are aware of the correct marker residue in the relevant matrices.

Ensure that the NRCP is implemented as planned, particularly in relation to the choice of matrix. The choice of analyte-matrix combinations should be rationalised and harmonised to ensure more comparability between the results from laboratories and consequently reduce the validation burden.

Ensure that each state CA issues uniform instructions to all samplers at district level in order to assure harmonised implementation of sampling within each state and put in place effective systems to supervise the implementation of NRCP activities.
Ensure that all states initiate follow-up actions in a timely fashion to improve overall effectiveness of implementation of residues controls as per Articles 16-19 of Council Directive 96/23/EC.
Ensure that all official residues samples are sealed in accordance with point 2.6. of the Annex to Commission Decision 98/179/EC and instructions in the NRCP.
Ensure that if PVPs are authorised to take official samples, measures are taken to eliminate potential conflict of interest.

Collate annual state sampling plans at CCA level to allow analysis of the 6 monthly reports in order to establish if the plan is being implemented as foreseen, and, if necessary, identify under-performing states and facilitate corrective measures to be taken. 8.3. With regard to the laboratories
Ensure that within laboratories, anonymity of sample ownership is assured in order to eliminate potential conflict of interest.

Ensure that all laboratories meet national and Community requirements with respect to validation of analytical methods, in particular demonstrating fitness for purpose. For Group A substances, provide a timetable for each laboratory indicating when each of the analyte matrix combinations for which they are responsible are expected to be validated to the standards prescribed in Commission Decision 2002/657/EC.

Ensure that basic quality control parameters are considered when analytical methods are run in every laboratory, including inter alia, establishing acceptance criteria for analytical data. 8.4. With regard to VMPs 18

audits.title: Fishery products and live bivalve molluscs

recommendations.text: Generalities related to CA FP/LBM control system performance Fishing vessels should comply with the requirements of Council Directive 92/48/EEC. The frequency of inspections carried out by the CA on fishing vessels and landing sites in order to verify their compliance should correspond to the one established by themselves and adequate numbers of staff to deal with this duty should be made available. The deficiencies found during the mission and not previously identified by the CA should be corrected in the establishments and dispatch centre visited and in all other establishments that were not visited but that may have similar shortcomings.

Live bivalve molluscs The classification of production areas should be amended according to microbiology results of monitoring. Provision for suspension in case of noncompliant results should be considered and possible conflicts of interest of the private entrepreneurs responsible for the collection of samples should be avoided. The NRL for microbiology should take contact with the Community Reference Laboratory in order to evaluate if procedures concerning the processing of samples (pooling and averaging) and interpretation of test data are appropriate. Further to this evaluation, the NRL should advise the state laboratories and the manual of procedures should be amended. Germany should respect the current Community requirements regarding the detection of marine biotoxins; therefore, in absence of validation of the chemical methods used, bioassays must be used. All the official laboratories performing chemical methods for the biotoxin identification should implement alternative detection methods able to detect DTX3. Adequate staff should be made available to the biotoxins NRL to enable it to adequately complete its assigned tasks. The deficiencies identified in laboratories, accredited by accreditation bodies, involved in official controls and own-checks should be rectified.

Fishery products Each batch of fishery products must be submitted for inspection (comprising an organoleptic check) by the CA at the time of landing or before first sale to determine, its fitness for human consumption. During production and before they are released for human consumption, fish and FP must be subject to a visual inspection for the purpose of detecting and removing any parasites that are visible in accordance with the requirements of Council Directive 91/493/EEC and Commission Decision 93/140/EEC. Whenever fish is sampled for official control of histamine, the sampling procedure to be followed by the CA should be the one required under Council Directive 91/493/EEC (nine samples must be taken from each batch). 19 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/7583/2005 A reply to the FVO letter dated 18 November 2005 (ref. 5, paragraph 1) was sent by the CCA informing that the competent Ministry of the Federal State of Schleswig Holstein has corrected the procedure of production area classification in order to comply with Community requirements. In their comments to the draft report, (letter of 22 February 2006, ref: 106-3612- 01/234738), the CA provided some details of corrective actions already undertaken and other planned actions, in particular: - Generalities: in MV the inspection system concerning fishing vessels has now been changed. All fishing vessels supplying approved establishments are registered as being subject to inspection. Every inspection is documented. - The frequency of inspections carried out by the CA of MV on fishing vessels and landing sites in order to verify their compliance was fixed at once a year on the basis of a risk assessment. - The deficiencies found during the mission and not previously identified by the CA have been partially corrected in the establishment listed as No. 3 in Annex III of this report (deadline was set for 30 June 2006 for remedying all deficiencies). Deficiencies found in establishments No. 1, 2 and in the establishment processing bivalve molluscs of Annex III have been rectified. - Live bivalve molluscs: in respect of recommendation 5.2.paragraph 3, the NRL organised validation of methods tests for PSP amongst the official laboratories in Germany in 2004. The results were discussed in December 2004 and the methodological instructions were revised in December 2005 and are to be published in the summer of 2006 as the official method in §64 LFGB (Food and Feed Code - Collection of Methods). The CCA referred as well to the comments on bioassay under point 2.2.2.1.f of the report. Furthermore, they stated that an enquiry as to the suitability of MBA was sent to the EFSA (EFSA-Q-2005-285). A reply is expected in December 2006. - In respect of recommendation 5.2, paragraph 4, the CCA pointed out that the detection of toxins in the DSP group, including DTX-3, is currently a priority in the § 64 LFGB working party on mollusc toxins. - In respect of recommendation 5.2, paragraph 5, the CA stated that priority has been given to remedying the shortage of personnel and optimising the installations. - Fishery products: in respect of recommendation 5.3.paragraph 1 and 2 the CA of MV stated that during routine inspections of fishing vessels, landing sites in wholesale installations or processing establishments the criteria for freshness of the fish are now being documented - In respect of recommendation 5.3, paragraph 3, the CA provided documentation confirming that instructions were given to comply with Community requirements (nine samples must be taken from each batch) in the three Länder visited. 11/04/06 - 55332

To ensure that animals slaughtered for human consumption, which have tested BSE positive in a rapid test and the one carcass before and the two following ones are destroyed in line with Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001. With regard to measures taken following suspicion/confirmation of BSE
To ensure that feeding cohort animals are destroyed as soon as possible, as required by Art. 13 of Regulation (EC) No 999/2001. With regard to the total feed ban
To ensure that all relevant risks are taken into account in the design of the control programmes, including the use of organic fertilisers, as required by Art. 3 (1a) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To ensure that the feed control programmes are also at regional or local level based on risk assessment. With regard to the laboratory network

To conduct the histopathological examination for all positive rapid tests or other positive test results, as required by Chapter III of Annex X to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001. 12 ADDENDUM RESPONSE OF THE COMPETENT AUTHORITIES TO THE RECOMMENDATIONS Comments from the German CA on the draft report were received on 23 June 2006, and included additional clarification and an outline of some actions planned and/or undertaken to address certai s contained in the report. These may be summarised as follows: With regard to BSE epidemio-surveillance 2. The CA of one Land visited advise the Commission that the Landesamt für Verbraucherschutz (Regional Office for Consumer Protection) is responsible to regularly organize an auditable training programme in accordance with Art. 10 of Regulation (EC) No 999/2001 for all the professional groups mentioned in that Article. 3. The CA of one Land visited advise the Commission that the listing of suspect cases in the annual report in accordance with Art. 6 (4) of Regulation (EC) No 999/2001 has been discussed with the CA and the laboratory and will be implemented accordingly. With regard to the total feed ban 6. The CA of one Land visited advise the Commission that in their opinion adequate attention is paid to fertilizers containing MBM during their inspections. They considered the introduction of a reporting system, which they rejected as they assessed the effort to be disproportionate. 13

audits.title: Animal By-Products

recommendations.text: To take steps to increase the level of awareness of the ABP Regulation among officials, including those responsible for supervising the district levels of the CA. With regard to the Legal provisions
To complete the changes necessary to bring the national implementing rules in line with the ABP Regulation. With regard to the approval of ABP plants and other premises
To take appropriate measures to complete the approval of ABP plants in accordance with the requirements set out in Chapters III and IV of the ABP Regulation.
To validate processing plants in line with Annex V to the ABP Regulation. With regard to official controls

To take appropriate measures to ensure a more consistent application of the official controls of the ABP chain at a frequency which takes account of the risks posed by each ABP plant, as required by Art. 26 of the ABP Regulation. The criteria used in preparing the control programme should set down in such a way as to enable the system to be monitored effectively.

To increase the level of coordination between the CA responsible for official control of the ABP chain as required by Article 4 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 in order to provide full traceability of ABP consignments which move between districts or Länder.

To ensure that all ABP are correctly categorised in accordance with the Art. 4. to 6 of the ABP Regulation, particularly by raising the awareness of the relevant requirements in officials and operators of food processing establishments.
To ensure full compliance with the requirement of Decision 2003/328/EC, in particular those concerning the type of material that can be used.

To take urgent measures to ensure the traceability of consignments of ABP along the ABP chain particularly by enforcing the requirements for commercial documents and other records laid down in Annex II to the ABP Regulation. __________________ 12 ADDENDUM RESPONSE OF THE COMPETENT AUTHORITIES TO THE RECOMMENDATIONS Comments from the German CA on the draft report were received on 11 July 2006, and included an outline of some actions planned and/or undertaken to address certai s contained in the report. These may be summarised as follows: With regard to the CA 1. The CA of one Land visited stated that officials had been provided with training on the ABP Regulation and that it was planned to carry out further training in December 2006 and in 2007. In addition, the CA provides monthly updates to take account of changes to the ABP Regulation. With regard to the legal provisions 2. The updated national implementing provisions for the ABP Regulation are currently being considered by the Bundesrat. With regard to the official controls 6. The CA of one Land visited is currently introducing a quality management system to all administrative levels in the Land to provide, among others, a framework for the organisation and planning of official controls and their supervision. 8. A list of different ABP by category is currently being discussed at Länder level with a view to making it available once it has been approved by legislative administrators. The CA of one Land visited has sent instructions to slaughterhouses and officials regarding the need to remove in the slaughterhouse the vertebral columns from half-carcasses of bovines aged over 24 months which are intended for use in petfood and to dispose of them as SRM. 9. Steps have bee taken to ensure the strict separation of former foodstuffs and catering waste intended for use in swill, including the clear labelling of containers used for their storage.

The CA of one Land visited noted that according to the curre of the agricultural committee as regards the ABP Compensation Ordinance (Tierische Nebenprodukte Bussgeldverordnung ­ TierNebV), the weight of ABP or number of carcasses, rather than the volume should be indicated in the national commercial document. ____________________ 13

audits.title: GMO - Controls of food and feed

recommendations.text: With regard to Third Country imports of foodstuffs within the scope of this mission, provide guarantees that these imports are subject to official controls at an appropriate place in accordance with Articles 15 and 16 of Council Regulation (EC) 882/2004 on official controls.

Should take account of Commissio 2004/787/EC also for sampling of feed for GMO analysis. An action plan in response to these recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission within two months of the dispatch of the report. This action plan should clearly set out the manner and deadline by which the competent authorities will address these recommendations. 10.
