In relation to Recommendation (2) the German authorities stated that an adaptation of the sampling procedure to Commissio 2004/787/EC is to be prepared for the whole of Germany.

audits.title: Import Controls - food and feed of non-animal origin

recommendations.text: Consider harmonising the frequency of sampling through all Länder for products listed under Article 55 of LFGB.
Ensure that all sampling procedures at import point are carried out in accordance with Council Directive 98/53/EC.

Comply with Article 1 of Commission Decision 2002/80/EC with regard to frequency of sampling for dried figs from Turkey. 21 To the Federal Ministry of Finance (1) Ensure, in line with Article 10 of the Treaty of the European Union, that Customs authorities are available to co-operate with Commission experts during the general and specific audits foreseen in Regulation 882/2004, in particular in order to allow them to verify the respect of the requirements of Article 24 (cooperation of competent authorities and Customs services). 11. COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS

audits.title: Intra Community Trade in live animals

recommendations.text: To ensure that official controls are carried out effectively and that corrective action is taken when needed, in accordance with the requirements of Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To implement proper procedures for administrative sanctions in respect of shortcomings found in assembly centres, dealers' premises, staging points, transport and business operators involved in intra-Community trade.
To introduce, without delay, internal audits as required by Article 4 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To ensure that audits or inspections of delegated bodies are organised and appropriate action is taken in case of non-compliance as required by Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To provide appropriate training for the official veterinarians performing official controls as required by Article 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To urgently review and strengthen the control procedures for assembly centres, dealers' premises, staging points, transporters and business operators involved in intra-Community trade and to approve only those which are fully in compliance with EU requirements.
To ensure that effective traceability systems are in place for horses, in particular those intended for slaughter. 21
To review the approval of the staging point visited and to take appropriate action to correct the deficiencies.

To ensure that checks are performed on live animals at their destination in accordance with the requirements of Article 5 of Council Directive 90/425/EEC, that the corrective actions set out in Article 6 of that Directive are applied if necessary and that the results of all checks are recorded in the manner prescribed by Commission Regulation (EC) No 599/2004.
To ensure that route plans are in compliance with Article 5 of Council Directive 91/628/EEC.
To ensure that certifying veterinarians comply with the requirements of Council Directive 96/93/EC and that checks or audits are carried out to ensure the integrity of certification.
To up-date the lists of approved assembly centres, staging points, dealers' premises and transporters.

To ensure that official controls on all holdings verify that stock farmers and veterinarians record and retain information on veterinary treatments as required by Annex I of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and Article 10 of Council Directive 96/23/EC.

To ensure that animals which have experienced pain or suffering during transport are slaughtered without delay in accordance with point I (6) of Annex A to Council Directive 93/119/EEC. 9. COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS

audits.title: Food Hygiene - Food of animal origin

recommendations.text: To issue the five Federal Decrees in order to ensure proper implementation of all parts of the EU hygiene legislation.

To put in place adequate procedures for co-ordination between the different levels of the control system (Federal, Land, Provincial and District level) including measures to improve the quality of information flows.
To update procedures and instructions in accordance with the new EU hygiene requirements in order to comply with the provisions of Article 4 (3 and 5) of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To implement audits of the CA as required by Article 4 (6) of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, to audit the identified control bodies within the meat sector as required by Article 5 (3) of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and to notify their activities to the Commission as required by Article 5 (4) of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To ensure the control bodies in the meat sector fulfil all requirements for control bodies before delegating official control tasks to them.

To consider the milk association as a control body with delegated tasks as laid down in Article 5 of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, to ensure it fulfils all requirements, to audit its activities and to notify it to the Commission.
To assess the reliability of the FBOs own checks and to include them in the assessment when organising the official controls, as required by Article 3 of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To develop and implement a system for verification of the effectiveness of official controls carried out as laid down in Article 8 (3) of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To ensure that a link between the certificate and the consignment is always established and that the information in the certificate is accurate and authentic as required by Article 30 of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. 25
To apply adequate control over the certificates issued in accordance with the provisions of Article 5 of Council Directive 96/93/EC.

To establish a system of review of the approvals of all establishments already approved, in accordance with Article 6 of Council Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, Article 3 of Council Regulation (EC) No 854/2004, and Article 31 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, including proper risk assessment and consistently applied inspection frequencies.
To audit the HACCP-based systems, to assess the results of the own checks, to verify the traceability and to document these official controls properly.

To introduce adequate control measures preventing the application of identification marks which are not in accordance with the provisions of Annex II, Section I (B)(7) of Council Regulation (EC) No 853/2004.

To introduce adequate control measures ensuring that animals at slaughter are completely bled after stunning in all cases in order to comply with the provisions of Annex D (2) of Council Directive 92/119/EEC.

To introduce adequate control measures of the labelling requirements of ABP in the meat and milk sector in line with the Council Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002. 7. COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS

audits.title: Identification/certification

recommendations.text: To inform the other Member States and the Commission of the identity of the Competent Authority responsible for ensuring compliance with the Regulation, as required by Article 11.

To communicate the details of the provisions for means and methods of identification, holding register and movement documents to the Commission as required in Article 4(8) and Section A of the Annex; Article 5 (6) and Section B(1) of the Annex; Article 6(5) and Section C(1) of the Annex, and Article 11 of the Regulation. 14

To grant the derogation in Article 4(1), second paragraph, of the Regulation, only to animals kept in extensive or free-range farming conditions and not to extend it to all sheep and goats in Germany.

To take into account specific provisions of the Regulation, in particular: ­ to ensure all sheep and goats are identified, as required in Article 4; ­ to approve the holding register format, as required in Article 5(3) and to ensure up-to-date registers, containing all information as listed in section B.1 of the Annex, are kept by each animal keeper as required by Article 5; ­ to ensure the movement documents as required in Article 6(1), are used; ­ all sheep and goat holdings are registered centrally as required by Article 7; ­ in the case of replacement of lost ear tags the objective of traceability is not compromised as required by Article 4(6); and ­ all mandatory information is available in the central database as required by Article 8(1) and Section D 1 of the Annex. 9. COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS The CA's partial response to the recommendations can be found at http://ec.europa.eu/food/fvo/ap/ap_germany_8208_2006.pdf. audits.title: Rabies eradication programme

recommendations.text: Consider that the recommendations made by the Scientific Committee concerning the monitoring of the effectivity of the immunisation are followed: · Consider that bio-markers are incorporated into the bait casing, so that bait uptake by the target species can be effectively assessed; · Consider that sufficient samples are tested for seroconversion in all Länder.
Ensure that serological and distribution data collected from the Länder are processed as quickly as possible to guide the further development of the eradication strategy.
Consider to take measures ensuring that the techniques used for routine diagnosis allow the detection of all possible vaccine-related rabies cases.

Consider that further inter-laboratory trials are organised for the official laboratories carrying out the tests for monitoring of rabies incidence (IFT and virus isolation in cell culture) and for monitoring of wildlife immunisation (RFFIT). An action plan describing the action taken or planned in response to the recommendations of this report and setting out a timetable should be presented to the Commission within two months of receipt of the final translated report. 10. ADDENDUM The German Authorities provided comments on the draft report by means of a letter dated 23 June 2006. Where appropriate these comments have been incorporated into the final report.

audits.title: Classical Swine fever

recommendations.text: To take measures to ensure the correct transposition of Council Directive 2001/89/EC and Commission Decision 2003/526/EC.

To ensure that the number of staff involved in the implementation of the CSF eradication and vaccination campaign is sufficient to allow all measures required in the Community legislation on CSF to be carried out effectively.

To ensure that the NPD covers the all districts, that all CA have access to it and to ensure that it complies fully with Art 14, point 3c of Council Directive 64/432/EEC to provide quick and reliable traceability in case of an outbreak.
To urgently ensure that CSF protective measures in relation to domestic pigs as required in Art 15 2 (b) and Art 6 and 7 of Commission Decision 2003/526/EC are implemented.
To ensure that the CSF vaccination campaign is carried out taking into account all provisions of Art 20, point 2 of Council Directive 2001/89/EC.
To ensure the withdrawal period for the CSF vaccine is taken into account in defining the hunting rest period after bait distribution.
To ensure that the recommendations 8.2 and 8.3 of report DG(SANCO)/7129/2004 are followed in relation to estimation of the feral pig population and bait distribution.

To ensure the correct implementation of Regulation (EC) No. 1774/2002 in relation to disposal of animal by-products in the game collection centres. The German competent authorities should submit an action plan indicating the action proposed or already taken, within one month of receiving the final translated report. This plan should include deadlines by which the proposed action will be completed. 10. Where appropriate these comments have been incorporated into the final report. 22

audits.title: Animal Welfare on Farms

recommendations.text: The requirement for laying hens for an uninterrupted period of darkness of about one third of the day, as required by point 3 of the Annex to Directive 99/74/EC is transposed in legislation.
Staff carry out and record checks correctly, using documented procedures, as required by Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No. 882/2004.
Verification of the effectiveness of inspections is carried out, as required by Article 8(3) of Regulation (EC) No. 882/2004 to ensure the quality and consistency of controls.

Written notifications for corrective actions are given where deficiencies are detected, as required by Article 54(3) of Regulation No. (EC) 882/2004 and that sanctions are effective, proportionate and dissuasive as required by Article 55(1) of Regulation (EC) No. 882/2004.

The data, as required by point 1 of the Annex to Directive 2002/4/EC, indicates the correct maximum capacity of the establishment. 17 9. audits.title: Food Hygiene - Food of animal origin

recommendations.text: To continue with their efforts in order to update the national legislation to ensure proper implementation of the EU hygiene legislation.

To continue with their efforts to improve the procedures for co-ordination between the different levels of the control system (Federal, Land, and District level) including measures to improve the quality of information flows, in 22 particular at lower levels, in order to comply with Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 Art. 4(3).

To continue with their efforts to update procedures and instructions in accordance with the new EU hygiene requirements in order to comply with the provisions of Article 4 (3 and 5) of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To continue with the efforts to implement audits of the CA as required by Article 4 (6) of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To take measures in order to ensure that the identified control bodies in the meat and milk sector in Bavaria and any other Bundesländer concerned are accredited, are subject to audit and to notify their activities to the Commission as required by Article 5 of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/200439.

To develop and implement a system for verification of the effectiveness of official controls carried out, in the Bundesländer where this is not in place, as laid down in Article 8 (3) of Council Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To provide the Commission Services with the results of the outcome of the investigation in relation to the certification of goods transiting from the Netherlands to Ukraine and take measures to prevent similar situations in all Bundesländer.
To take measures to ensure that the official controls are carried out regularly on a risk basis and with appropriate frequency in all Bundesländer as foreseen in Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 Art. 3.
To ensure that reports are drawn up after official controls in line with Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 Art. 9, and when needed provide the FBO with a copy of the report.

To introduce adequate control measures preventing the application of identification marks which are not in accordance with the provisions of Annex II, Section I (B)(7) of Council Regulation (EC) No 853/2004.

To take measures in order to ensure that the controls on raw milk production are fully compliant with Annex IV, chapter II (1) of Regulation (EC) No 854/2004. An action plan describing the action taken or planned in response to the recommendations of this report and setting out a time table, and a description of the actions taken to correct the deficiencies found should be presented to the Commission within 25 working days of receipt of the report. 10. audits.title: Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathies (TSE) in sheep and goats

recommendations.text: To ensure that the epidemio-surveillance monitoring targets set out in Chapter A, II (2a and 3) of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001 are complied with.

To ensure genotyping of the minimum sample size of animals required by Chapter A, II (8.2) of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001 and that the sheep sampled are representative of the whole sheep population. 9
To ensure that SRM is correctly removed as required by Annex V to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001.
To document the official controls on SRM as required by Article 8 (1) and 9 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. ____________________ COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS

audits.title: Import Control system for products of animal origin and live animals

recommendations.text: To immediately cease the activities in the proposed BIP as long as it is not listed in the Annex to Decision 2001/881/EC in accordance with Artt. 6 of Directive 91/496/EEC and Directive 97/78/EC. With regard to legislation and administrative measures: (deadline for completion: 3 months of the receipt of the translated final report, as required by Art. 6 of Decision 2001/812/EC)

To continue the development of administrative measures for adequate implementation of Art. 6, 8, Annex II of Directive 97/78/EC, Annex A of Directive 91/496/EEC, Decision 2001/812/EC and Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.
To ensure that requirements for inspections fees foreseen according to Art. 27 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and Decision 97/132/EC are adequately implemented.

To draw up procedures or finalise the manual of procedures to ensure that veterinary checks are carried out and veterinary decisions are taken in accordance with the requirements laid down in Directives 91/496/EEC and 97/78/EC and harmonisation of procedures with other BIPs is ensured.
To further develop the system to ensure that all relevant documentation are provided to all BIPs and records are kept as required by paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 of the Annex to Decision 2001/812/EC.

To ensure that consignments of products of animal origin and live animals (e.g. CITES) are introduced only through BIPs having the appropriate approval in accordance with Art. 3 of Decision 2001/812/EC and Art. 3 of Directive 97/78/EC and Art. 3 of Directive 91/496/EEC.

To clarify the responsibilities for checks on non-commercial pets and birds and products of animal origin in personal baggage of travellers from third countries and supplement the measures taken to better implement the requirements laid down in Regulation (EC) No 998/2003, Decision 2007/25/EC and Regulation (EC) No 745/2004 respectively. With regard to supervision/management of the system: (deadline for completion: 3 months of the receipt of the translated final report, as required by Art. 6 of Decision 2001/812/EC)

To improve co-operation and co-ordination with the other authorities involved for import controls and to develop a system for the identification and selection of the consignments of veterinary interest, especially regarding access to all manifests and electronic systems for the analysis of relevant intelligence, as 11 laid down in Artt. 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 and Artt. 5 and 6 of Regulation (EC) No 282/2004.
To improve the control system for import controls and BIPs to ensure compliance with Art. 8 and 9 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and improve verification of corrective action taken.

To monitor staff resources at BIP level to ensure that sufficient staff are available to comply with the provisions foreseen in the Annexes to Directives 91/496/EEC and 97/78/EC, in particular in view of the number of consignments expected.

To monitor, if the provided training is adequate and to finalise the training plan for 2008 to ensure that the relevant officials avail of initial and ongoing training in import controls in order to fully apply Art. 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To further develop the systems for documentation of the destruction of kitchen waste, including seized POAO in personal baggage, to ensure that the requirements for collection, transport and records for their destruction are implemented as laid down in Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002. With regard to the infrastructure of the proposed BIP Leipzig-Halle visited:

To correct the shortcomings of the proposed BIP regarding facilities, equipment and hygiene in order to comply with the requirements of Directive 97/78/EC, Decision 2001/812/EC and Directive 91/496/EEC. With regard to the import control system: (deadline for completion: 3 months of the receipt of the translated final report, as required by Art. 6 of Decision 2001/812/EC)

To ensure that pre-notification is received in advance of physical arrival of the consignment in the Community territory as required by Art. 2 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 and Art. 1 of Regulation (EC) No 282/2004, Art. 3 (1) of Directive 91/496/EEC and Art. 3 of Directive 97/78/EC.

To ensure that in the electronic information systems used by Customs the positive list of Decision 2007/275/EC is applied adequately to ensure fulfilment of the requirements of Art. 3 (4) of Directive 97/78/EC in relation to the presence of the CVED.
To ensure that the channelled procedure and monitoring of consignments are applied in accordance to Art. 8 (4) of Directive 97/78/EC.
To ensure that the monitoring sampling plan will be completed in accordance with Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 136/2004.

To ensure that shortcomings in procedures are rectified in particular in relation to prior authorisation required in accordance to Art. 16 (1e) of Directive 97/78/EC so that such consignments are not being marketed. 12 9. COMPETENT AUTHORITIES' RESPONSE TO RECOMMENDATIONS The competent authorities' response to the recommendations can be found at: http://ec.europa.eu/food/fvo/ap/ap_germany_7917_2007.pdf

audits.title: Specific audit on animal by-products (ABP) and on gelatine

recommendations.text: To ensure compliance with the requirements of commercial documents and records, as set out in Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002.

To ensure compliance with the hygiene requirements for the collection and transport of ABP and processed products in slaughterhouses and cutting plants, as set out in Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002 (Chapters other than III and IV), in particular as regards identification of bins and mesh size for sieves.

To continue taking measures to complete the approval of all ABP plants in accordance with the requirements set out in Chapters III and IV to Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002, including technical plants like tanneries, and to ensure that they figure on the list of ABP plants.

To notify the Commission of the premises in Germany that are authorised to use derogations for ABP and the verification arrangements put in place in accordance with Art. 23 (3) of Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002.

To reinforce official controls on former foodstuffs at retail and wholesale level to ensure compliance with the requirements of Regulation (EC) No 197/2006, in particular records of consignments. With regard to the gelatine sector

To ensure that all plants supplying raw materials for the production of gelatine for human consumption are registered or approved within the food chain, as required in Chapter I (4) of Section XIV of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 853/2004.
To ensure segregation of food grade and ABP grade hides dispatched from slaughterhouses to hide plants, as set out by Chapter I (5) of Section XIV of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 853/2004.

To comply with the requirement for the documentation of hides destined for the production of gelatine intended for human consumption, as required by Chapter II (1) of Section XIV of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 853/2004 13

audits.title: Specific audit to evaluate import/transit controls and border inspection posts

recommendations.text: To review and amend national public and animal health law to ensure correct transposition of Artt. 6 and 11 of Directive 97/78/EC and Art. 3 of Directive 91/496/EEC, of the technical Annexes to these two Directives and implementation Art. 2 (1) of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004.

To further develop adequate administrative arrangements and review all instructions and manuals for veterinary procedures to ensure compliance with the provisions laid down in Directives 91/496/EEC and 97/78/EC and the implementing Regulations and Decisions, also Regulation (EC) No 1/2005, and to provide clear guidance as required by Art. 8.1 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 in order to facilitate and ensure correct implementation of veterinary checks and animal welfare. To establish a clear procedure for approval/suspensions for BIPs as provided for in Artt. 6 of Directive 91/496/EEC and 97/78/EC. 24

To review lists required under Art. 13 of Regulation (EC) No 998/2003, Artt. 8 (6) and 12 (4) of Directive 97/78/EC, Chapter XI of the Annex to Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002 to ensure the publication of the most recent versions and to formalise the list required by Art. 2 (3) of Decision 2007/25/EC.
To continue the corrective action for the list of entry points for CITES- consignments to bring it into line with the BIPs listed in Decision 2001/881/EC.

To ensure the use of the TRACES system in accordance with Decision 2004/292/EC and that correct and complete information is entered into TRACES in accordance with the aforementioned Decision and Regulations (EC) No 136/2004 and 282/2004 and to update the registration systems in place to ensure that all the information required under Decisions 97/152/EC and 2001/812/EC is maintained.
To take measures to ensure that all documentation is maintained at the BIPs as required in accordance with section 3 of the Annex to Decision 2001/812/EC.

To implement measures in accordance to Articles 3 of Directive 91/496/EEC and Directive 97/78/EC to ensure that notification is provided in advance of the arrival of the consignment on EU territory as required by Regulations (EC) No 136/2004 and 282/2004.

To crosscheck if all relevant CN codes in the electronic system for processing Customs formalities (ATLAS) are included with a link/flag in relation to the requirement of a CVED to ensure adequate implementation of Art. 7 (3) of Directive 97/78/EC.

To take the measures necessary to ensure that the exchange of information and access to databases or parts thereof as required in Artt. 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004 and Artt. 5 and 6 of Regulation (EC) No 282/2004 is put in place at BIPs for the relevant consignments ensuring that the requirements of Artt. 3, 9 and 11 of Directive 97/78/EC are fulfilled.

To take further measures to ensure that veterinary checks, the veterinary decision and the follow up of specific consignments are implemented fully in line with the requirements of Directives 91/496/EEC and 97/78/EC and of Regulations (EC) No 136/2004 and 282/2004.

To take into account the findings of this report in development future training programmes for all staff performing import controls on POAO or live animals, including pet animals in BIPs or customs entry points in order to better apply the provisions of Art. 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To take further measures to ensure the correct application of the requirements laid down for non-EU-complying consignments laid down in Artt. 9, 11, 12 and 13 of Directive 97/78/EC and Decisions 2000/208/EC and 2000/571/EC.

To take further measures to ensure the correct application of Regulation (EC) No 745/2004, especially regarding information to travellers and to Customs control staff and adequate destruction of any seized POAO in order to fully implement the provisions laid down in Artt. 3 and 4 of this Regulation as well as relevant provisions in Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002.

To take further measures to ensure the correct application of the requirements laid down for checks on non-commercial pet animals laid down in Regulation (EC) No 998/2003 and Decision 2007/25/EC, in particular in relation to the checks carried out and the information provided to the public or official staff responsible for carrying out the controls. 25

To take further measures to ensure that the requirements for supervision, collection, transport and records for destruction of kitchen waste from international means of transport are implemented as laid down in Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002.

To rectify the deficiencies and shortcomings noted for the facilities, equipment and operational hygiene in the BIPs visited in order to implement the provisions of Directives 91/496/EEC and 97/78/EC and Decision 2001/812/EC.

audits.title: Specific audit on residues and contaminants in live animals and animal products, and veterinary medicinal products

recommendations.text: To ensure that effective risk-based official controls and supervision of the handling of ABP/DP, as required by Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009, are carried out in all federal states in order to enable the competent authorities to better verify that the relevant traceability requirements for ABP/DP are fulfilled throughout Germa (d, e, f), 15, 16, 17 and 26.

citations.text: The organisation of official controls remains largely as described in the country profile (see section 4.1). Within their territories, each of the 16 federal states has exclusive competence for the organisation, planning and execution of the official controls and supervision of ABP/DP required by Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009.

There were a number of important differences in the approach taken in the two federal states in the organisation, planning and performance of official controls on the ABP/DP chain and so these are covered separately: The following was observed in Bavaria: a. A system of risk-based official controls for ABP/DP plants and operators has been put in place, as required by Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 which takes into account a number of criteria to determine the basic frequency of official controls (above a set minimum) to be carried out. With the exception of one transporter, all 4 plants and operators visited by the audit team in Bavaria had been inspected at least as often as established in the risk-based control plan. b. This federal state has put in place relevant checklists and guidance, which help to ensure that points relating to traceability and commercial documents are taken into account during the routine official controls carried out in the ABP/DP chain, in accordance with Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009. These documents were being used in practice in the plants visited. c. Staff met by the audit team were aware of the relevant requirements for documentation and traceability of ABP/DP and the reports of the inspections performed were sufficiently detailed to show that the requirements regarding commercial documents and traceability set down in Articles 21 and 22 of Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009, respectively, had been checked. The results of these inspections were entered into a database which, according to the competent authority, provides a means to monitor that the official controls are carried out regularly in accordance with the risk-based programme, set down in accordance with Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. The following was noted in NW: d. In contrast to the situation seen in Bavaria, the district authorities, rather than the federal state, are responsible for planning the official controls. The audit team noted that insufficient measures have been put in place by the federal state which could help ensure that each of the district authorities carried out this task consistently and appropriately, in accordance with the criteria set down in Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. Deficiencies in this respect were evident, as neither the transporter of ABP/DP nor the storage facility for derived products visited by the audit team had been subject to official controls as the district authority had not established an inspection frequency for these operators. In another case, a district authority had classified traders and transporters as being a low-risk activity irrespective of the categories and volumes of ABP/DP which they were handling, or if any risk of cross- contamination were present. As a result, it cannot ensure that official controls of the ABP/DP chain in NW are carried out in accordance with the requirements of Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. e. Similarly, in the absence of any measures, such as checklists or guidance, being put in place at the federal state level, the district authorities are also responsible for deciding what should be checked during official controls. A lack of relevant checklists for transporters of ABP/DP and producers of OF/SI at district level was given as one of the reasons why the operators referred to in point (d) above were not subject to official controls. f. Information provided by the competent authorities prior to the audit showed no non- compliances relating to traceability of ABP/DP were identified in the last two years in the establishments to be visited in NW. However, given the range of shortcomings identified by the audit team in the ABP plants visited which were overlooked during 5 official controls (see points 16, 17, 18) this raises doubts about the ability of the competent authorities to ensure that the correct handling of ABP/DP, including requirements for traceability and commercial documents, are verified regularly i

The system in place for the organisation, planning and implementation of official controls of the ABP/DP chain relies largely on the federal states putting in place adequate measures to ensure the relevant EU requirements are fulfilled. However, in the absence of measures to encourage a harmonised approach to these tasks, substantial differences were seen in the two federal states visited. While one (Bavaria) had put in place a mostly satisfactory system of risk-based controls for most operators in the ABP/DP chain, many deficiencies were identified in the effectiveness of the systems put in place by the districts authorities in the other federal state visited (NW) and there were insufficient measures in place to enable these to be identified and corrected either by the federal state or by the competent authorities. This issue, combined with the fact that paper traders of ABP/DP are neither registered nor subject to official controls, undermines the ability of Germany to ensure that all relevant operators in the country are subject to regular official controls, carried out in accordance with EU requirements, to verify compliance with the traceability requirements for ABP/DP.

Although operators generally make efforts to comply with the traceability requirements for ABP/DP, there is a lack of consistency in the performance of official controls on these aspects, which, in one federal state visited resulted in deficiencies being overlooked. This also applies to the use of TRACES, consignments handled by paper traders or those traded to and from other Member States where there is limited information available regarding their fate. These factors undermine the ability of the competent authorities to ensure that operators fully comply with the traceability requirements for ABP/DP throughout the country. 10

recommendations.text: To ensure that all operators active in the ABP chain, notably paper traders are subject to official controls, as required by Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009.

citations.text: Representatives of BMEL informed the audit team that traders which are shown in the commercial documents as being the final destination for ABP/DP even though they do not actually receive the goods (hereafter: paper traders) have not been registered in accordance with Article 23 of Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009 as this activity is considered to be outside the scope of the ABP Regulations. In the federal states visited, such traders were not included in the scope of official controls on the ABP/DP chain.

In all plants visited, operators were aware of the requirements relating to the registration or approval of their suppliers or customers. The inspectors carrying out official controls in the plants visited were actively cross-checking that the operators and plants shown on commercial documents (including those located in other Member States) were approved or registered as required. The audit team checked the registration/approval status of several operators appearing on commercial documents and noted that all but the paper traders were registered or approved in accordance with Articles 23 or 24 of Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009, respectively.

The system in place for the organisation, planning and implementation of official controls of the ABP/DP chain relies largely on the federal states putting in place adequate measures to ensure the relevant EU requirements are fulfilled. However, in the absence of measures to encourage a harmonised approach to these tasks, substantial differences were seen in the two federal states visited. While one (Bavaria) had put in place a mostly satisfactory system of risk-based controls for most operators in the ABP/DP chain, many deficiencies were identified in the effectiveness of the systems put in place by the districts authorities in the other federal state visited (NW) and there were insufficient measures in place to enable these to be identified and corrected either by the federal state or by the competent authorities. This issue, combined with the fact that paper traders of ABP/DP are neither registered nor subject to official controls, undermines the ability of Germany to ensure that all relevant operators in the country are subject to regular official controls, carried out in accordance with EU requirements, to verify compliance with the traceability requirements for ABP/DP.

At a storage plant for derived products visited in NW, the audit team noted that several consignments of horn chips which, according to the operator, originated in a third country, were received without being accompanied by a commercial document. These consignments were found to have been imported by a trader based in a federal state other than the ones visited in this audit, and then stored in a different federal state before being dispatched to the plant in NW without commercial documents. This is not in line with the requirements laid down in Annex XIV, Chapter II, Section 12 of Regulation (EU) No 142/2011. This issue had not been identified during the official controls performed in the federal states involved.

According to data extracted from TRACES by the audit team, in 2013 approximately 8,570 commercial documents notifications were sent to Germany from several Member States and the arrival of around 5,470 (64%) of these consignments was confirmed. Consignments entering Germany via traders were not confirmed in TRACES as traders are not registered and not subject to official controls. In 2014, data extracted from TRACES show that approximately 3,000 (30%) out of 10,000 consignments arriving in Germany were confirmed. This does not fulfil the requirements of Article 48(3) of Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009.

recommendations.text: Ensure that laboratories for pesticide residue analyses in organic products are part of the official laboratory network and these are communicated to 2. the National Reference Laboratory in order to facilitate the activities specified in Article 33 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004. Ensure that existing instructions and/or procedures regarding: (a) sampling for pesticide residues in organic products (b) criteria set out for methods of analyses, i.e. selection of laboratories, and (c) rules on the interpretation of results are based on methods fit for the intended purpose or developed in accordance with scientific protocols, as required by Article 11(1) of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004; these should be sufficiently checked by the relevant CA(s) in order to guarantee that controls at organic operators are effective and these are performed in a consistent manner, as laid down in Articles 4 and 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004 and Article 9 of Regulation ((EC) No 834/2007.

citations.text: In Germany, organic samples taken by CBs are analysed in laboratories for pesticide residues. There is no legal obligation for CBs to notify these laboratories. Therefore, this is not a pre-condition for their approval. As part of the approval, CBs are only requested to inform the CA about laboratories they use, but these are not officially assessed by the CA. Furthermore, no legal requirements are in place for these laboratories to be officially designated. As a result, their use for purposes within the scope of the audit is not communicated to the NRLs, and, thus these laboratories are not subject to supervision by either the NRLs or the approving CA.

As laboratories for analysis of organic samples under Regulation 834/2007 are not designated by CA and communicated to the NRLs, they are not included in the co- ordination of and supervision by NRLs and EURLs, which can influence the quality of analytical results.

audits.title: Salmonella National Control Programmes in particular poultry populations

recommendations.text: The CA should ensure that, for the implementation of the SNCPs, the interpretation of the term flock is in line with that of Article 2.3. (b) of Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003. In particular the CA should ensure that the sampling protocols applied are in line with EU requireme

citations.text: The identification of the bids of a holding is based on the specific populated house of the holding (house number) and the date it is populated or the age of birds. Under the actual interpretation of a flock, even where birds are kept in different houses on a holding, in some instances they can be considered as a single flock equating with one epidemiological unit. The audit team noted that usually all the birds of the populated houses of the same holding being in the same location are considered as one epidemiological unit and so as one flock (e.g. 7 houses with a common egg belt of a laying hen farm were documented as one flock). This does not match with the EU definition of a flock which in the case of housed poultry is deemed to be all birds sharing the same airspace according to Article 2.3. (b) of Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003. The CA further informed the audit team that the Länder guidelines refer to Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003 for the flock definition.

In particular, the CAs at Länder level explained that in order to establish the size of a flock, several factors are taken into consideration (e.g. common equipment used among holding's houses, common hygiene facilities and common entrance into the houses, other risks of cross-contamination). Based on this, the CA representatives in NI informed the audit team that in the majority of cases each holding represents a single flock. 9

However, the audit team noted during its visits to different holdings that in some cases houses equipped with their own hygiene facilities (separate entrances for each house of the holdings, separate ventilation systems, separate silos for storage of feed and feeding systems) and located close to each other were considered as one flock.

In relation to the actual interpretation of flock, when the audit team reviewed the implementation of the SNCP during its visits in the different districts offices and poultry farms, it was noted that: in the majority of cases reviewed, the sampling protocols applied by the FBOs were in line with EU requirements. In these instances, even if all the houses of the holding had been considered as one flock, the sampling protocols of own-checks were applied per house. in a small number of cases reviewed, the interpretation of flock led to less samples been taken by FBOs. In three holdings examined (one turkey fattening farm and two laying hen farms) the own-checks sampling comprised one pair of boot swabs per house instead of two. In these cases the sampling protocol was applied per flock (consisting of more than one house). as according to EU and federal legislation the own-check sampling is based on flock, the FBO is not always obliged to follow the sampling protocols required by EU legislation (in cases that one flock comprises more than one house). For example, the audit team noted in a turkey farm visited that the sampling instructions sent by the CA instructed the FBO to take two pairs of boot swabs per flock. As the flock consisted of five houses that meant that these tests could be taken from one only house. The audit team further noted that based on his own initiative the FBO was applying this sampling protocol to each of the houses. The CA on the spot informed the audit team that in this case the FBO, by his own initiative, carries out more samples than what he is obliged to under federal rules. the official actions taken in cases of Salmonella infections were not always consistent and were based on a case by case decision by the district authorities. In some of the districts visited the audit team was informed by the CAs that when one house of a holding is found Salmonella positive, official actions (further official sampling, restrictive measures, etc.) would be applied to all the other houses as they comprise one flock. However, in other districts visited the CA view was different: official actions were applied only to the infected houses5. In the Länder visited the audit team was informed by the CAs that no specific guidelines/instructions explaining the actions to be taken in these situations have been issued at federal or Länder level6. in some cases the number of flocks of a holding was communicated to the CA by the farmer and is checked later during official controls. The audit team noted that 5 In their response to the draft report the CA noted that official actions were applied only to the infected houses where these comprise a single flock. For this purpose, an epidemiological assessment is required in each case. 6 In their response to the draft report the CA noted that this is always a case-by-case decision which is determined by local conditions and the type of management (biosecurity concept, personal hygiene, etc.) on the farm concerned. Official measures are nevertheless based on, inter alia, § 9, § 10 and § 11 GflSalmoV. 10 in most instances there was no official documentation kept on the farm or in the district offices regarding the number of flocks defined in each holding (only information about the number of the populated houses of the holding).

The interpretation of the term flock used by the German authorities does not always match the definition set down in EU legislation. As a consequence, the testing scheme in place cannot ensure that the sampling protocols applied always meet EU requirements.

The audit team visited two laying hen holdings. The first one consisted of two houses keeping two different flocks: one free range and one in enriched cages. The second holding consisted of three houses, with a barn farming system, considered to be one flock according to the actual interpretation of flock definition. During the visits at the local CAs of both Länder visited the audit team also reviewed documentation related to other laying hen farms. During these visits and the reviews the audit team, noted that: · the sampling frequency of official and FBO sampling were in compliance with EU legislation with the exception of one case where the first sampling of the adult laying hens had been delayed for six weeks. This shortcoming had not been 19 detected during official controls. The inspectors on the spot explained to the audit team that no recent official control had been carried out on the implementation of the SNCP (regarding this specific flock). · the sampling protocol applied: o for official routine sampling was in line with EU requirements and the SNCP o as part of own-checks was incorrect in two of the farms examined (e.g. one pairs of boot swabs instead of two). In one of these two farms the CA explained to the audit team that the five houses of the holding were considered to be one flock (see also third point of paragraph 39).

The implementation of the SNCP for the laying hens is, in general, carried out in accordance with the programme and EU requirements, in particular concerning sampling frequency of the official controls and of the own-checks and sampling protocol used during routine official sampling. However, the sampling protocols applied by FBOs when the holding consists of different populated houses are not always in line with EU requirements, particularly due to the actual interpretation of flock's definition.

recommendations.text: The CA should ensure that, in breeding hen flocks, confirmatory sampling policy complies with Point 2.2.2.2 (c), Annex to Regulation (EU) No 200/2010 and that the sampling protocol used in confirmatory sampling is in line with Point 2.2.2.2 (b) of the Annex to this Regulatio

citations.text: Under federal legislation and SNCP rules, confirmatory testing must be always performed when own-check tests, taken at the holding or hatchery, result positive for the targeted Salmonella serotypes. The practice of performing routine confirmatory sampling when own-checks results of sampling at the holding are positive is not in line with Point 2.2.2.2 (c) of Annex to Regulation (EU) No 200/2010 which establishes that this should only be done in exceptional cases, when the CA has reason to question the test results (e.g. false positive or false negative results).

Under federal legislation and according to the information given to the audit team by the CA, confirmatory sampling (at holding level) is carried out in accordance with Point 2.2.2.2 (a) of Annex to Regulation (EU) No 200/2010 (i.e. sampling protocol provided for official routine sampling) by taking one set of samples in accordance with Point 2.2.2.1 of the Annex to the Regulation. However, the Regulation states that in the exceptional cases described in Point 2.2.2.2.(c) of its Annex the sampling should be carried-out in accordance with Point 2.2.2.2.(b) (i.e. official protocol for confirmatory sampling following detection of the relevant Salmonella serotypes from sampling at the 17 hatchery). According to the third paragraph of Point 2.2.2.2. (b) if Salmonella is not confirmed at this stage, antimicrobial testing shall be carried out or new bacteriological testing for the presence of the relevant Salmonella serotypes shall be carried out on the breeding flock or their progeny before trade restrictions can be lifted. The confirmatory sampling protocol in accordance with Point 2.2.2.2 (a) applied by the German CA is not in line with these EU requirements as in case of negative analysis results (for the relevant Salmonella serotype) the flock is considered negative and no further antimicrobial testing or bacteriological testing is carried out.

The confirmatory sampling policy applied in holdings is not in compliance with Point 2.2.2.2 (c) of Annex to Regulation (EU) No 200/2010 as it is carried-out without any specific reason to doubt the validity of the initial results (false positive or false negative results). In addition the sampling protocol used is not in line with Point 2.2.2.2 (b) of Annex to Regulation (EU) No 200/2010, particularly concerning the lack of furter testing when the presence of relevant Salmonella serotypes is not confirmed.

recommendations.text: The CA should ensure that in laying hen flocks:- - Confirmatory sampling policy complies with Point 4, Part D, Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003. - The sampling protocol used in confirmatory sampling is in line with the one described in Point 4, Part D of Annex II of Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003. - The absence of the use of antimicrobials potentially affecting the results of the analyses of the sampling is verified. - All flocks of adult laying hens within the framework of the SNCPs shall be covered by the sampling frame as required in Point 1 of Annex to Regulation (EU) No 517/2011.

citations.text: In both Länder visited the audit team was informed by the CAs that specific criteria had been developed for the assessment of these quality systems implemented at farm level. The CCA informed the audit team that the GflSalmoV requires also authorities at district level to report the data (e.g. the number) of these holdings. However, in two of the four district offices visited the audit team noted, that this data was not reported and that official controls to verify/monitor the implementation of the conditions to be met in these holdings had not been performed. The audit team further noted in the districts visited that the number of these holdings were in general low. The fact that the sampling frame does not cover all laying flocks within the framework of the SNCPs provided for in Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003, and particularly concerning the lack of FBO sampling in some flocks, represents a non-compliance with Point 1 of Annex to Regulation (EU) No 517/2011. However, according to § 9 and § 21 of GflSalmoV when there is a suspicion of an infection with relevant Salmonella serotypes, specific preventive measures are taken by the CAs in these holdings.

According to the GflSalmoVand the SNCP, an official confirmatory sample has to be always carried out in case an own-check sample results positive for the Salmonella targeted serotypes (or if there are sufficient grounds for suspecting a Salmonella infection for the targeted serotypes e.g. after the detection of relevant serogroups). This is not in line with EU legislation (Point 4, Part D of Annex II of Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003) as it should only be carried out in exceptional cases in order to exclude initial false-positive results.

In two of the districts visited the audit team noted that the sampling protocol applied during the confirmatory sampling was the same as that for routine official sampling (three pair swab tests instead of five boot swabs plus two dust samples analysed separately) and so it is not in line with Point 4, Part D of Annex II of Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003.

The audit team further noted, in all the positive cases examined, that the serotyping (for both own check and official samples) was always carried out officially in the NRL, which needed a usually long time to provide official results (see also paragraph 61). 20

In all the Salmonella positive cases examined by the audit team, it was noted that no laboratory tests for verification of the absence of use of antimicrobials was performed by the CA when confirmatory sampling resulted negative. This is not in line with Point 4, Part D of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003 which requires CAs to verify11 the absence of use of antimicrobials, potentially affecting the results of analysis of the sampling. The CA informed the audit team that this verification is based on documentary checks. In one of the districts visited the CA informed the audit team that it is not foreseen, as part of the SNCP, to take samples for detecting the use of antimicrobials. Conclusions on SNCP for laying hens

A small number of holdings under the framework of SNCPs (with number of birds <1000) can under certain conditions be excluded from the Salmonella sampling frame. This could have an impact on the level of Salmonella prevelance reported by Germany as the number of these holdings is not always reported by the local CAs and there are no data on sampling results.

The confirmatory sampling policy applied in Germany, which is performed routinely without any specific reason to doubt the validity of the initial test results is not in line with the relevant EU legislation. In this regard the sampling protocol used does not comply with Point 4, Part D of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 2160/2003, in particular concerning the method used, which is less sensitive than the one required in this Regulation. Furthermore the actions taken for verifying the absence of the use of antimicrobials potentially affecting the results of the analysis of the confirmatory sampling do not comply with EU rules either.

recommendations.text: The CA should ensure that the routine confirmatory sampling in broiler flocks is not performed as this is not in line under Regulation (EU) No 200/2012.

citations.text: According to federal legislation, confirmatory sampling must always be performed in case of results of own-check sampling being positive for relevant Salmonella serotypes. This is not in line with EU requirements.
The confirmatory sampling policy in place, which is performed routinely, is not in line with the relevant EU rules.

recommendations.text: The CA should ensure that the food chain information document provided in Section III of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 853/2004 contains all the relevant information in order to comply with third paragraph of Point 4.2 of Regulation (EU) No 200/2012. When AMI takes place at holding the CA should ensure that the official responsible of the inspection takes appropriate measures as regards the 7. communication of inspection results (e.g. to include relevant information in point 4 of the health certificate provided for in Part A, Chapter X, Section IV of Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 854/2004) in order to meet the requirement of Article 5(3) of the same Regulatio The CA should ensure that, for breeding turkey flocks, the confirmatory sampling policy is only carried out when the conditions set out in Point 2.1(b) (i) second indent of Annex to Regulation (EU) No 1190/2012 are met. The CA should ensure that in fattening turkey flocks the routine confirmatory sampling is not performed as this is not in line under Regulation (EU) No 1190/2012.

citations.text: In the districts visited, the audit team reviewed documentation on broiler flocks found positive for relevant Salmonella serotypes. The CA informed the audit team that: · In one case, the FCI and the health certificate (signed by the official veterinarian when the AMI was carried out at the holding of provenance) did not contain information on the Salmonella status of the flock despite the laboratory results being positive for Salmonella targeted serotypes, and · In a second case, in another district, despite a routine official sample result being positive for Salmonella spp, neither the FCI nor the health certificate contained this information. The flock was slaughtered as Salmonella negative, based on a negative own-check sample taken subsequently (the day following the official sampling day). The official serotype results were received from the NRL after the birds were slaughtered and were positive for Salmonella targeted serotypes. · In both cases the CA notified, informally via phone, the FBO of the slaughterhouses about the Salmonella history of the flocks.

The CAs explained to the audit team that the health certificate template does not contain a specific point for reporting information on Salmonella results /status of the flock12. The CA also added that the FBO is obliged to include positive laboratory results in the FCI. It may include negative results at its discretion.

The above mentioned findings are not in line in particular with: · third paragraph of Point 4.2 of Regulation (EU) No 200/2012 which states that the results of the tests shall be considered relevant for the FCI as provided in Section III of Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 853/2004, and · The requirement of Article 5(3) of Regulation (EC) No 854/2004 which requires the official veterinarian who carried out inspection tasks to take appropriate measures as regards the communication of inspection results.. Conclusions on SNCP for broilers

The control system in place does not ensure that the relevant information concerning Salmonella in broilers is provided as required along the food chain through in particular the FCI and the health certificate accompanying birds to the slaughterhouse which are found to be Salmonella positive.

Veterinary checks generally ensure that only eligible consignments are accepted for transit.

recommendations.text: To ensure that controls at the warehouse are implemented in line with the EU requirements laid down in Decision 2000/571/EC and Directive 97/78/EC.

recommendations.text: To implement actions to ensure that CVEDs issued for non-conforming consignments leaving approved customs warehouses are cross referenced to the original incoming CVEDs as required by Article 1(6) of Decision 2000/571/EC.

citations.text: In their response to recommendation No 1 from report DG(SANCO)/2013-6901 (described in finding 36), the competent authority stated that: Super Local Veterinary Unit (SLVU) accounts would be made available to competent authorities issuing CVEDs for non-conforming consignments leaving approved warehouses, and written instructions would be provided in the form of frequently asked questions on the TRACES administrator's (FLI) website. 13 Both these actions had been completed but no SLVU has issued a CVED in Germany at the time of the audit. The competent authority presented to the audit team the missing functionalities in TRACES as the reason for failing to use it.

In relation to the issuance of subsequent CVEDs in the warehouses, the audit team noted that: in warehouse 1 the exiting consignments were not accompanied by subsequent CVEDs, therefore there was no documentary traceability of the goods. This is a consequence of the absence of an official control system in warehouse 1 contrary to the requirements of Article 12 of Directive 97/78/EC; in warehouse 2 the consignments were intended for ship supplies and left accompanied by the veterinary certificates in compliance with the requirements of Article 5 of Decision 2000/571/EC; the representative of another Land, in which the audit team did not visit a warehouse, stated that the subsequent CVEDs accompanying consignments exiting the warehouse are created in COACH. They have the reference number of the original ("mother") CVED in box 11 under "Documentary reference". When the interface transfers information into TRACES, the CVEDs appear as new transits and the link between entering and exiting split consignments is lost.
The actions proposed to address recommendation No 1 from DG(SANCO)/2013-6901 have not been effective and the recommendation remains unaddressed.

audits.title: Xylella fastidiosa

recommendations.text: Ensure that a national contingency plan is established for the control of Xylella fastidiosa by 31 December 2016, as required by Article 3a of Commission Implementing Decision 2015/789/EU.

citations.text: At federal level, preparatory steps have been made under the leadership of the JKI for developing a contingency plan for Xf. A working group was set up with participation of diagnostic and plant health control experts from Bavaria, Thuringia, Brandenburg, Baden-Württemberg, North Rhine-Westphalia and Lower Saxony.

The intention of the CAs is to elaborate a national contingency plan with annexes, dealing with the specific conditions of each Land. The first draft has already been prepared and it concentrates on the provisions for establishing the DA. The future steps 4 include the elaboration of the details of the plan, consultation with professional organisations and discussing this with the CAs of the Länder to obtain their agreement for publication and implementation.

The audit team noted that: Some elements of the existing contingency plans in Saxony and Thuringia are in line with some provisions of Article 3a of Decision 2015/789/EU. However, the plans cannot be considered as meeting the requirements of the Decision; It is unlikely that the national contingency plan will be finalised by 31 December 2016, the deadline set by Article 3a of Decision 2015/789/EU. 5.1.4 Communication and cooperation within the plant health services and with other authorities involved in controls
The delayed elaboration of the national Xf contingency plan may impact negatively on the implementation of the necessary measures in the case of possible future outbreaks.

recommendations.text: Ensure that in the buffer zone, in the framework of the annual surveys, visual inspections take place in each square of the grid split into 100m x 100m squares as required by Article 6(7) of Commission Implementing Decision 2015/789/EU.

citations.text: The LPPS of Saxony and Thuringia carried out surveys in the BZ, based on a grid split into 100 x 100 m squares, as required by Article 6(7) of Decision 2015/789/EU. At the time of the audit, Saxony had inspected 1,394, while Thuringia 2,535 squares, 9% and 16% of the squares in the BZ in their territory, respectively.

The 2016 surveys stopped in mid-October, because the appearance of autumn leaf colours made the recognition of symptomatic plants impossible. The audit team noted that due to the staff shortage and the available time the CAs were not able to complete the surveillance according to the provisions of the EU Decision.

The presence of Xf in the BZ was monitored with a methodology, in line with EU provisions and the most risky sites were prioritised. However, as the entire territory of the BZ was not checked, the absence of Xf has not yet been fully verified.

recommendations.text: Ensure that official controls on the movement of specified plants guarantee the implementation of provisions of Article 9(1) of Commission Implementing Decision 2015/789/EU.

citations.text: The audit team noted during visits in nurseries and garden centres in the BZ that the operators: All have stocks of specified plants and market them all year around; Grow or keep the specified plants in open field or in non-vector-proof establishments; Do not carry out vector controls, the applied chemicals target the main pests of the plants, but not the xylem feeding vectors; Usually do not have detailed inventories of the specified plant stocks, their origin and time of arrival; Do not register their customers, however they stated that they are usually from the area and are informed about the movement restrictions; Are fully aware of the details of the EU legislation, including the list of host and specified plants, but they do not verify that the destination of their specified plant sales is in the BZ.

The audit team also noted that: LPPS inspectors of Saxony and Thuringia carry out some controls on the movement of specified plants in the nurseries and garden centres in the BZ; The customers of the nurseries and garden centres are not checked and no road controls are carried out; The implementation of movement restrictions relies mainly of the extensive public awareness measures (see chapter 5.5.1 and 5.1.5). The audit team therefore considers that the official controls cannot ensure that plants which have been grown for at least a part of their life in the DA are not moved out of that area. Conclusions on the movement control of specified plants

The implementation of movement restrictions relies mainly on public awareness. Little actual control of the sale/movement of specified plants takes place and the level of guarantee foreseen in the Decision 2015/789/EU may not be achieved.

recommendations.text: To ensure that import manifests are checked at the BIPs Munich and Leipzig as required by Articles 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004.

citations.text: At BIP (and DPE) Leipzig, 98% of consignments are handled by the same operator who provides information concerning consignments prior to arrival for both products of animal and non-animal origin. For this operator, import manifests are checked by the official staff on a daily basis. No checks of manifests by the official staff or alternative systems are in place at the BIP for consignments handled by the other operators, which is not in line with Articles 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) 136/2004. The competent authority informed the audit team that corrective actions will be initiated to include these checks on the consignments handled by the other operators (2%).3 2 In their response to the draft report, the competent authority noted that they agreed to this procedure because the freight companies and the authorities have different working hours. 3 In their response to the draft report, the competent authority noted that consignments from passenger aircraft have to be registered through enquiries with the airline. Measures are being agreed with the airlines at Leipzig 6

At BIP Munich, checks of manifests have not been carried out by the official staff since 2014 contrary to the requirements laid down in Articles 6 and 7 of Regulation (EC) No 136/2004. The competent authority stated that a new IT tool is being developed to include such checks. It is planned that this system will be finalised and implemented by end 20164. Conclusions on the mechanisms to ensure that consignments are presented for import controls

Mechanisms are in place, supported by the system applied by the Customs authorities, to ensure that consignments requiring enhanced controls are presented for official controls. In one BIP visited such a mechanism is still under development and does not yet ensure that all consignments subject to enhanced controls will be identified.
